chapters.title: Chapter 751 - 751. Another Floor
paragraphs: Finally, after what seemed like an aimless exploration, they entered the tunnel where the boss room was located.
"Myne, the boss... it seemed, had already been defeated."

While Myne was looking at the five-meter-tall iron door, which was wide open and further covered in thick darkness from which nothing could be seen, Aisha, beside him, who was holding a map, spoke with a serious expression.

He turned his head to her, and looked her up and down, before reaching his hand inside her skirt when the others weren't paying attention and pinching her soft, bubbly buttocks hard with an expressionless face.
"I can see that too. You don't have to tell me such useless nonsense with that serious expression."

Basically, what she said was a fact that even an idiot knows. The mechanism of a boss room inside a dungeon is very simple: when the giant door is closed, it means the boss is inside, and you should be prepared for battle. Once someone enters, it will be locked immediately.
Then, after defeating the boss, the lock automatically unlocks, and the door opens by itself.
The door remains open until the boss respawns, before closing, so new death-seekers know that someone is waiting for them inside.

"You... I will deal with you tonight. You're becoming more and more of a rascal!" Aisha, whose buttocks were hurting because Myne had pinched too hard, hit him on the head with the map and whispered angrily.
But just as Myne was about to continue teasing Aisha, Sylphy, who had gone to investigate who might have entered the boss room ahead of them, came back and shook her head.
"There are no footsteps or anything around here that could give us any clue as to who or how many people are inside."

"Let's forget about it and let's move forward. Maybe it's an adventurer party that came to grab the first clear reward. I've heard that the first clear reward of any new dungeon is very generous, and since it's been quite some time since this new dungeon opened, it's very normal for those greedy adventurers to find this place," Myne said calmly.

He had heard stories about adventurers doing anything for profit and reputation. There were once rumours that an adventurer party, in order to grab the first clear reward of a high-difficulty dungeon, killed an entire town because they needed a lot of time to clear that dungeon, and the townspeople wanted to publicly release information about that dungeon to everyone so the town could attract tourists and other adventurers and gain profit from it.

"What if there's a demon inside? You know, the location of this dungeon is very hidden, and unless someone has a special skill or is extremely lucky, it's not easy to find it. But it's a different story for demons, I heard, that they can sense nearby dungeons," Aisha asked thoughtfully while rubbing her chin.

"If there's a demon inside, just beat him down. Anyway, I haven't seen any demons from our world. This way, at least I finally have a chance to meet one," Myne didn't take this seriously at all. To him, demons or anything from his world were no longer something he focused on; they were just too weak compared to the dangers outside his world.

"By the way, since the boss was defeated, how long will it take for the boss to respawn?" He asked Aisha. Since he has already come to this dungeon for a picnic, he doesn't mind grabbing some new skills. The skills of dungeon bosses are quite rare and useful, and it's been a while since he has acquired any new skills.

"Hm, it depends on the dungeon... But I think this dungeon would take a longer time. The time it takes for a boss to spawn depends on the amount of mana stored inside a dungeon. The more mana, the faster it is for the boss to spawn. This dungeon was recently made; it's still in a state where mana isn't accumulated in huge quantities."
"Since mana density is very low here, generating a new boss is obviously going to be a very tough task for this new dungeon."
With much greater experience in exploring dungeons and having access to a huge source of information from the Adventurers' Guild, Aisha shared her opinion after a moment of thinking.
"That makes sense."
Everyone nodded at Aisha's explanation.

Since the boss wasn't going to respawn anytime soon, they didn't waste time and quickly walked into the boss room, ready to move to the next floor. Because dungeon monsters are special, and most of the time after they are killed, they just vanish into thin air, leaving a bunch of loot behind for their killer, there were no dead bodies or blood on the ground of the boss room, and it was neat and clean.

Myne and his group casually looked around to see if there was anything that could provide them with information about the people who came before them. Finding nothing, they went directly to the floating magic crystal at the end of the boss room. Touching it would teleport them to the next floor, which was the first basement floor.
Basement First Floor

"It looks exactly the same. As expected, there's nothing new here," Myne, who had been looking forward to a new floor because he was tired of seeing the dark, cave-like interior of the dungeon, shook his head in disappointment.

This was also the reason why, after visiting a few dungeons in his free time with his girls, he never personally took the initiative to go there for levelling up. First of all, most dungeons seemed to be made by someone who was too bored and just copied and pasted them; you could find countless similarities in each dungeon that matched other dungeons.

Second, most of the monsters were the same—like goblins, slimes, orcs, ogres, trolls, some small insect monsters, etc. It was very rare to find new, unique, never-before-seen monsters—at least in the dungeons in the Aguesta Kingdom. Myne had never seen any kind of dungeon monster that could make people pee in their pants just by looking at it.

And finally, their level. Most dungeons were very low-level ones with only a few floors; their monsters, loot, and everything else were very ordinary and low-level, which could only attract the attention of ordinary adventurers. There was nothing thrilling or life-threatening that could make a high-level individual's blood boil just by hearing about it, forcing them to leave everything behind and come to clear that dungeon.

"This floor is the same. I can't sense any mana here as well," Waffle, who was casually floating around, spoke while shaking his head. Although he wasn't a picky guy, he actually didn't like low-density mana zones much; he felt a little uncomfortable and suffocated there.

"Maybe there's something wrong with this dungeon. Otherwise, no matter how low-level or newly born this dungeon is, the mana density here shouldn't have fallen to a nearly extinct point," Aisha spoke with a frown. But because she had never encountered such a problem, she didn't have any clue about it and could only advise others to be vigilant.

Although the mana density was close to none, the monsters inside the dungeon didn't seem to have any problem in this kind of environment. Only after walking for a few minutes, Myne and the others encountered another group of new monsters.
[ Name: Lion
LV: 16
Race: Lion Race ( Faithfulness and Felidae Family )
Gender: Male
[Skill]
Strong Arms ( Large )
Cooperation Telepathy ( Short Distance )
[Ability]
Biting ]

"Wow, it's a White Lion. I had no idea there would be a lion inside a dungeon. By the way, why do all the monsters in this dungeon seem to have an intense love for white colour?" Myne joked while looking at the new skill with a hint of curiosity.
[ Cooperation Telepathy (Short Distance)
Description: Those who have this skill can telepathically talk to each other. However, the range is limited to a 3-meter radius.
Cooldown Time: None ]

"Hmm, although I have Fenrir', and other divine beasts' telepathy skills, their use is very limited. But this skill is also useless; it only has a 3-meter radius. If I have to talk to someone within such a short distance, can't I just call them out? Sigh, hopefully, this floor boss has an updated version of this skill.
Shaking his head, Myne applied this to himself, his two wives, and their pets, before explaining its uses to them.

"Good! With that, we can finally talk with Ocea! I always wanted to talk with her properly, but because we don't have her mother's blessing, we can't talk with her. But with this skill, that problem is finally solved!" Aisha said with brightened eyes, looking as if she would rush to Ocea deep in the mana ocean if she could.
"Ohh, yes, I almost forgot about this!" Sylphy nodded excitedly. "But now, why don't we move our muscles? I'm feeling itchy after wandering in this cave for so long without doing anything."

After that, without Myne saying anything, with a tactical understanding, everyone rushed toward the group of lions and started killing them. Since the power difference between both two parties was too huge, it was nothing but a one-sided massacre.

chapters.title: Chapter 752 752. Leftovers
paragraphs: "Phew, we finally reached the boss's room. Why are there so many lions on this floor? It's as if the dungeon has consumed all its energy to produce them. Though they are weak and easy to kill, they are so annoying, continuously jumping around, disturbing my work."

Aisha complained while drawing the map. This was also part of their mission; having a map could help other adventurers and forces clear the dungeon more efficiently. Since Aisha was the only one who could do it, being continuously interrupted naturally put her temper in a bad state.
Thankfully, they had arrived at Floor B1's boss room, and now she no longer had to see those lions again.

"As expected, the door to the boss room was open," Seeing the huge door wide open, Sylphy, who was most looking forward to a good battle, couldn't help but sigh regretfully. The next moment, her face turned hideous as she was truly pissed off.
"Calm down, honey, it's just a random boss. We can always kill one; there's no need to be so angry, it's not good for your skin."

Myne, seeing that his other wife's temper was also heading in the wrong direction, quickly tried to calm her down. But to tell the truth, he also wasn't in a good mood. Although he didn't care about the meagre loot from a low-level dungeon, it didn't mean he liked picking up someone else's leftovers.
"This is definitely the work of adventurers. Those bastards seem to have already found out about this place," Aisha cursed while slamming her foot angrily.
"Why do you think so? Didn't you say it was the work of a demon?" Myne asked confusedly; he couldn't understand why she had changed her train of thought.

"Because why would a demon need to explore a dungeon in the first place? The way we were going would lead us to the inner depths of the dungeon where its core is located, which is useless to demons since most of the time it is their work to plant those cores and create dungeons so they can build their monster army and create trouble for other races."
"Since it can't be a demon, the only one left is obviously us, humes."

Instead of Aisha, it was Sylphy who took the lead and explained seriously, the fire of anger in her eyes becoming even more intense. She seemed about to turn into a demon for those poor adventurers who illegally entered the dungeon.

"There was such a big signboard outside saying that it is a forbidden dungeon and no one is allowed to enter it, but those greedy bastards never listen. Today I am going to cut all of them to pieces; only then will they take the royal family's words seriously."

"Ahm, honey, I don't want to ruin your mood further, but why are you caring about royal family matters so much? Don't forget you are no longer part of them. Yes, they are your family too, but the kingdom's affairs and what they do have nothing to do with us," Myne spoke calmly while patting her shoulder, bringing Sylphy back to her senses.

Hearing his words, she first showed a confused expression before understanding what Myne was trying to say. After getting married to a commoner, she had lost all her authority as a princess or someone from the royal family. Now she was nothing but a commoner's wife. However, because of Myne's teleportation skill and Garnet and Ayri always being around, Sylphy had forgotten about those things and was still stuck in the time she was a princess.
"Well, you are right. I think I still haven't been able to move on from my past identity," Sylphy replied with a worried smile, hugging Myne for some comfort.
After a moment of drama, and Myne and Aisha working together to reboost Sylphy's morale, they all entered the boss's room.

"I feel bad about not encountering this level's boss. I was hoping to get the advanced version of the Telepathy skill. The one given by normal white lions only has a reduced effect of 3 meters, which is a bit too short of a distance," Myne shook his head regretfully as he walked into the empty, dark boss room and came to the floating teleportation crystal, which would send them to the next floor.
"Don't worry, we can come back here tomorrow when the boss respawns," Aisha comforted Myne, making his mouth twist.

There was no way he would spend another of his precious days wandering around doing clan missions and exploring those low-level dungeons with them. Today's first clan mission alone had already eaten away all his patience; it was already a miracle he hadn't run away until now, and holding on.
Basement Second Floor.
"MYNE! I can feel it, the mana, it is back! There's a lot even! Wow, a mana-rich environment is so good and refreshing," Waffle floated around and spoke in excitement.
"Great, since you can sense mana, then what about the boss? Can you sense its location?"

Because Waffle had shown great talent in being a boss detector before, and Myne was no longer in the mood to waste any more time in those maze-like cave structures of the dungeon, he asked without wasting a single second.
"Leave it to me! I will definitely find it!"
"It's finally time for the show to begin," Sylphy answered excitedly, touching the hilt of her sword with an evil smile.
Aisha, who no longer had to run everywhere to complete the map, also smiled happily.

"Myne! I've found it! It's over there! In that cave, quickly follow me! This time, we have to reach the boss room before those people who went ahead of us," Waffle spoke seriously. It seemed like Sylphy, he also wasn't satisfied enough and wanted to try his paws on someone strong.

"That's awesome, Waffle! What are you guys waiting for? Let's go! Do you again want to be left behind by those bastards?" Sylphy spoke excitedly and quickly ran forward with Waffle, gaining great momentum.
"She is definitely sad. You shouldn't have said that," Aisha shook her head, watching Sylphy try to hide her sadness behind her fake excitement.

"But she has to face the truth. She can't just make a joke of a princess despite not being one. Not only will people not appreciate her work, but they will also criticize her for messing around and poking her head into others' business. It is better to hurt a little now than a lot later," Myne didn't feel he had done anything wrong by showing Sylphy reality.

He put his arm around Aisha's shoulder, gave her a quick kiss, and continued, "Don't worry about her. I have a dozen ways to light up her mood. You take care of your temper. When you get angry, I feel I am getting more anxious and worried, fearing that you might jump on me and vent your anger."

"Hey, what did you say? Are you calling me an abusive wife? Am I not caring and kind-hearted enough?" Aisha, hearing Myne's joke, played along and instantly grabbed his ear and twisted it hard, showing him what a real abusive wife looked like.
"Sorry, sorry, it was just a joke, ouch, ouch, it hurts, be gentle, Aisha!" Myne pretended to be in great pain and jumped into Aisha's arms like a child, not stopping until she let go of his ear.
"Don't you dare to anger me, otherwise you know the consequences," Aisha said while narrowing her eyes, but only after three seconds, she burst out laughing, watching Myne's fake crying.
"You really know how to make me happy," She spoke with a smile and gave him a hard, passionate kiss before looking forward.
"Look, there's a new type of monster!"
[ Name: Bee
LV: 22
Race: Lion Race (Faithfulness and Insect Family)
Gender: Male
[Skill]
Guaranteed Hit
[Ability]
Poison Needle
Paralysis Needle ]

"Hmm, a swarm of giant bees, not bad, but... we've reached the third level of the dungeon. Aren't monsters still a bit too weak?" Myne, who was used to fighting monsters with unusual power levels, couldn't accept the fact that there could also be places where monsters appeared according to their level sequence, instead of randomly overpowered monsters popping up to f*ck them up.

"But those bees' skill seem quite useful! With this, we don't have to worry about not hitting the target... But it can't be as overpowered as I'm thinking," Muttering such, Myne first pasted "Guaranteed Hit" on himself. After choosing a target, he turned around and shot a fireball in the opposite direction of the target, and as he expected, the fireball hit the cave wall.

Then he turned back and shot a fireball only a few inches away from the target bee, and this time, the skill took effect, and the fireball automatically moved in the air as if it knew where its target was and accurately hit the back of the bee, burning it to death.
"So this is it: if the attack wasn't too far from the target, this skill forcefully moves the attack and hits the target."

While explaining the skill effect to Aisha, whose eyes instantly lit up as this skill was nothing but a must-have skill for any archer like her, he pasted this skill to everyone and saved a few on stones on the ground, deciding to give his other girls this as well.

I have a dozen ways to light up her mood.
You take care of your temper.
When you get angry, I feel I am getting more anxious and worried, fearing that you might jump on me and vent your anger."
"Hey, what did you say?
Are you calling me an abusive wife?
Am I not caring and kind-hearted enough?" Aisha, hearing Myne's joke, played along and instantly grabbed his ear and twisted it hard, showing him what a real abusive wife looked like.
"Sorry, sorry, it was just a joke, ouch, ouch, it hurts, be gentle, Aisha!" Myne pretended to be in great pain and jumped into Aisha's arms like a child, not stopping until she let go of his ear.
"Don't you dare to anger me, otherwise you know the consequences," Aisha said while narrowing her eyes, but only after three seconds, she burst out laughing, watching Myne's fake crying.
"You really know how to make me happy," She spoke with a smile and gave him a hard, passionate kiss before looking forward.
"Look, there's a new type of monster!"
[ Name: Bee
LV: 22
Race: Lion Race (Faithfulness and Insect Family)
Gender: Male
[Skill]
Guaranteed Hit
[Ability]
Poison Needle
Paralysis Needle ]
"Hmm, a swarm of giant bees, not bad, but... we've reached the third level of the dungeon.

Aren't monsters still a bit too weak?" Myne, who was used to fighting monsters with unusual power levels, couldn't accept the fact that there could also be places where monsters appeared according to their level sequence, instead of randomly overpowered monsters popping up to f*ck them up.
"But those bees' skill seem quite useful!
With this, we don't have to worry about not hitting the target...
But it can't be as overpowered as I'm thinking," Muttering such, Myne first pasted "Guaranteed Hit" on himself.
After choosing a target, he turned around and shot a fireball in the opposite direction of the target, and as he expected, the fireball hit the cave wall.

Then he turned back and shot a fireball only a few inches away from the target bee, and this time, the skill took effect, and the fireball automatically moved in the air as if it knew where its target was and accurately hit the back of the bee, burning it to death.
"So this is it: if the attack wasn't too far from the target, this skill forcefully moves the attack and hits the target."

While explaining the skill effect to Aisha, whose eyes instantly lit up as this skill was nothing but a must-have skill for any archer like her, he pasted this skill to everyone and saved a few on stones on the ground, deciding to give his other girls this as well.

chapters.title: Chapter 753 - 753. Chess Piece
paragraphs: "Sylphy! Need any help?!"
Myne shouted out as Waffle and Sylphy found themselves surrounded by a large swarm of one-meter-tall giant bees, seemingly in big trouble.
"No need!"
Both of them called out together before using all their firepower to deal with the hundred or so giant bees surrounding them.

"Although the monster level of this dungeon isn't high, the quantity is quite huge. Suppose someone with limited strength gets surrounded by them. In that case, even if they are powerful enough to kill a dozen alone, it won't take long for the noise of battle to attract other nearby monsters, leading to them getting overwhelmed and dying," Aisha said seriously while firing arrows, watching more bees emerge from other cave entrances and join the battle.

"Indeed, but what I'm worried about right now is that the noise we're making is too loud and might alert those people ahead of us. I really don't want to see another empty boss room," Myne said with a frown.
"Now you can take action."

Finally, after nearly five minutes of nonstop battle and seeing no hope of killing all the seemingly unlimited bees, Sylphy and Waffle returned to Myne's side. Sylphy wiped the sweat from her forehead and spoke. There was no embarrassment on her face for wasting so much time or alerting their enemy just because she was feeling bad and wanted to find someone to vent her anger.

"Sigh, you guys are such troublemakers," Shaking his head, Myne snapped his fingers, and two giant red hexagram arrays appeared on the ground in front of them. As the bees got close, two pillars of fire shot out from the arrays, large enough to touch the cave ceiling, burning all the bees near them to ashes.

But since there were more bees ahead, Myne didn't stop there. He first created three wind tornadoes, made them pass through the fire pillars, creating giant fire tornadoes. While maintaining mana output so those fire tornadoes didn't dissipate, he let them move forward and clear their path.

"I thought I heard someone talking about making less noise so we don't alert our enemies?" Aisha taunted him, rolling her eyes, as she watched Myne use skills powerful enough to destroy an entire dungeon floor.

"What else can I do? Sylphy's previous high-profile action was more than enough to alert them. So what's the point of pretending as if they don't know about us and continuing to be low-key? Isn't it better to do our best and move forward as quickly as possible? Maybe we'll reach the boss room before them?" Myne replied with an innocent smile and a shrug of his shoulder.
"Myne, we're going to arrive!... However, it seems like those people are still ahead of us and have already gone inside to challenge the boss," Waffle's voice was full of disappointment.
"What bad luck. Seems like after hearing the noise, they sped up their exploration as well," Aisha shook her head. She had already expected this outcome when Sylphy started making trouble.

"What should we do next? Wait for them?" Sylphy felt sorry for her mistake, but there was nothing she could do about it. At that time, she was too emotional and urgently needed something to vent, so now she could only try to change the topic.

"Otherwise? Unless you can open this door forcefully somehow, or we return home and come back tomorrow, there's nothing we can do except wait," Myne tried to open the door with brute force, but it didn't budge an inch.

"But at least there's good news: as soon as the door opens, we can get inside and finally meet those bastards. I can't wait to have a nice chat with them," He continued with a smile, and others also had expressions similar to his. Obviously, everyone was looking forward to meeting those hard-working people.

After that, everyone sat down near the door and started having lunch. Normally, at the entrance of a boss room, it is deemed a safety zone. So, no monsters came to bother them, and they enjoyed their picnic.
However, maybe their luck was good, or they were just unlucky. They had barely taken a few bites of food when, with a loud rustling sound, the boss room door opened.

"Damn it, can't those bastards waste a few more minutes?" Myne put down the sandwich in his hand with an unwilling expression as Aisha and Sylphy, like hot-blooded chickens, had already stood up and walked toward the boss room. Obviously, they were more interested in catching their opponents than leisurely eating lunch with him.
Complaining, Myne got up, packed everything, and quickly caught up with them, but to his surprise, he found them standing at the entrance of the boss room with no intention of moving forward.
"What's wrong?" He asked while poking his head out from behind them, but seeing the thing that stop them, he was also left dumbfounded.
"Is that a figure covered in blood lying down there?"

Although his eyesight was the best among everyone in his group, he still didn't want to believe his eyes at the scene he was seeing. He asked with a frown because he recognised the person on the ground, and if possible, he didn't want to meet him in any good condition and stay as far from him as possible.

The figure of one adventurer, who was covered in blood and collapsed near the left wall, was seen by everyone. If not for the fact that the lighting in the boss room was good, and they could see his chest moving, by the amount of blood he lost, it would be easy to mistake him for a corpse.
"Isn't it the guy who caused trouble at the clan opening ceremony yesterday? Should we check on him?"

Although Aisha usually didn't mind saving people if she could without getting into any kind of trouble, for Merlin, who left a very bad impression during the clan opening ceremony and forced them to kick him out of the clan, she only had one thing for him: that middle finger.
"Let's go, take a look, but if possible, we better not get involved with him. This person is nothing but a trouble-attracting magnet," Myne said with a frown on his face.

He walked toward Merlin, who was badly injured, with a heavy claw mark on his back deep enough to show his bone. If not for the fact that Myne knew this guy was a chosen one and carried a maxed-out luck attribute, and was more difficult to kill than a cockroach, he would have thought he was seeing a miracle.

If I remember correctly, after dying, this guy can resurrect within a one-kilometre radius, right? So technically, for him, dying is a much better option than getting injured and falling into a coma, which wastes a lot of his time.

But with the amount of luck he has and the care he gets from the world's will, since he's not dead but in a coma, which is a very rare case given how badly he's injured, maybe there's a reason behind all of this... It can't be because the world's will wanted him to get close to me, right?

Otherwise, it's a bit too much coincidence that after I threw him so far away from the centre of the kingdom, he still managed to come back to the capital city within one day and even somehow managed to get involved in the exploration of a dungeon that was unknown to most people.
Why am I smelling a scent of conspiracy from all of this, as if someone is manipulating everything behind the scenes?

As he thought all of this, Myne felt a chill run down his entire body. There's no way anyone likes to be arranged like a chess piece, especially when you're not the protagonist and just a side character who can get replaced at any moment.
"Myne! Myne..."
Myne, who was in deep thought, feeling anxious and wondering whether he should run to Fenrir to get some advice about this matter, had his thoughts interrupted by Waffle's loud voice.
"What?!" He replied irritably.

"Look, that damn bird is here too; it seems she's about to die as well," Waffle, who was right opposite them near the left wall, answered happily. The moment he met Cynesuke, he never liked this bird, who was the number one asslicker of her master, who was a big idiot.

"So? You want me to heal her?" Myne, who didn't want to have anything to do with Merlin or his pets and was thinking about how to get him away from his ass, didn't understand why Waffle was telling him about his bird.

What did it have to do with him if that bird died or not? Yes, he acknowledged that the bird was indeed very rare, but her character obviously had a big problem, and he didn't like her behavior of being a complete bootlicker of her stupid master. Her master didn't care about her, but she was willing to do anything for him. According to him, such a foolish bird would rather die than waste air in this world.

chapters.title: Chapter 754 - 754. Screw the Script
paragraphs: "So? You want me to heal her?" Myne, who didn't want to have anything to do with Merlin or his pets and was thinking about how to get away from him, didn't understand why Waffle was telling him about his bird.

"No, I was just informing you. If you don't want to help them, then let's move forward. It's not like she's my friend or something," Waffle shook his head casually, uncaring about Cynesuke's life or death, and flew back to Myne and the others.

"Then what should we do about them? Ignore this idiot and his bird and continue catching this guy's other teammate?" Sylphy, feeling uncomfortable by the awkward silence while watching someone die before her, couldn't help but ask. She didn't know why Myne hated this guy so much, as a supportive wife, sometimes she didn't need to know the reason for doing what Myne said.
"Wait a minute, I'm thinking," Myne closed his eyes and replied absentmindedly.

Although he really wanted to ignore this bastard Merlin, the Chosen One, what he feared was that this move might anger the will of the world, and as a result, his luck would hit rock bottom, causing him to suffer bad luck for some time. After all, by not playing the role of a supportive character as he should in the Chosen One's journey, he was indirectly messing with the world's plans.
"Damn it..."
A minute later, Myne suddenly cursed, jolting everyone as they didn't expect such a reaction from him.

"Forget about those two, just ignore them. Since they didn't care about their life and death before exploring an unknown dungeon, why should we care about them? We are not their parents," said Myne." Saying that, Myne didn't hesitate anymore and walked toward the teleportation crystal.

Although it was true that he didn't want to anger the world's will, this also didn't mean that he would become its chess piece. He was powerful enough to handle any kind of danger in his world, so he could take the risk of getting unlucky, but there was no way he could let anyone control him like a puppet.
"Al... alright..."

The others also looked at each other before following him. Although they felt sorry for Merlin and Cynesuke, since Myne didn't want to help, they weren't going to fight with him for some strangers. And Merlin obviously hadn't left a good impression on them before, when he made trouble during the clan's opening ceremony.

After Myne and his gang teleported to the next floor, in the boss room, only Merlin and Cynesuke remained, lying on the cold floor, half-dead. But this didn't last long, as soon after, Merlin lost his breath. His body started glowing with a red light.

With a whoosh sound, his body suddenly vanished from its spot and reappeared at the entrance of the B2 floor. To his surprise, as the red glow faded away, all of Merlin's injuries had healed. The deadly poison in his body was also clear, as if it had never been there in the first place.

"F*ck! It hurt like hell," Merlin cursed with his eyes wide open, holding his stomach. Although he was fully healed, because of his skill's side effect, which gave him pain from which he died for the next 3 seconds, of course, after enhancing it multiple times so he could remember the feeling and learn from it, it was more than enough for him to remember his enemies' seven generations.

"Cynesuke! Damn it, hopefully, she won't die; otherwise, the loss will be unimaginable. I've already lost my two rare monsters; if Cynesuke also dies, I'll have nothing left and will have to start everything from the beginning," Thinking so, Merlin, after recovering from the pain, hurriedly rushed toward the boss room. Thankfully, his memory was good, and he remembered the route; otherwise, he would have wasted a lot of time before reaching his destination, and by then, his pet's body would have long ago turned cold.

"Those f*ckers! Just you wait. If I don't kill every one of those bastards, I'll change my name. And those bastards called their clan 'family,' 'family' my ass. They are nothing but a group of hyenas, ready to eat each other as soon as they find the chance... Even that b*tch was no different from the others, and I thought she loved me, damn gold digger."

While cursing and regretting letting down his guard against those so-called friends of his, Merlin, with some tears in his eyes from receiving such a heartbreaking level of betrayal, quickly came to the boss room. After looking around, he soon found his pet, Cynesuke, a mysterious bird-type monster he found in an inheritance site of a big guy, and who had been with him from the day it was born.
Merlin hurriedly picked up Cynesuke and put his ear near her chest to check whether she was still breathing or had already gone to meet her ancestors.

Thankfully, his luck was good, and she wasn't dead... At least not until Merlin realised that his belongings were also stolen by his dear friends and girlfriend. Now he didn't have anything he could use to heal his pet.

Because he had a skill that made him immortal, he was always very careless about injuries and didn't carry anything on him, just casually throwing some potions in his storage pouch, which he was now regretting. If he had known about it earlier, he would definitely have carried some healing potions in his pocket.

To make matters worse, Merlin, who was barely running to the teleportation crystal, wanting to leave the dungeon, suddenly heard a loud metal object moving sound, and the shining blue crystal before him also turned grey, obviously becoming offline.
"You've got to be kidding me."

He said with a depressed expression as he turned back and saw a giant hexagram magic array appear in the middle of the boss room, and the entrance door had also closed tightly. With an eye-blinding white light, a giant white bee, 5 meters in size, appeared in the room, staring at Merlin with a not-so-friendly expression.

Although usually after defeating a boss monster in a dungeon, it doesn't respawn anytime soon, but because this is a new dungeon and mana density in lower floors is many times higher than above, and it had been nearly an hour since the boss was defeated, and to rub salt on Merlin's injuries, it had respawned again at a critical moment, sealing his hope of rescuing his dear pet.
"AHHHH!!!"

Ten minutes later, Merlin again teleported to a random corner of the dungeon, this time on the B1 floor. Although physically he was completely fine and at full health, there was no longer any light of hope in his eyes. After the pain of being stomach-pierced by a giant sting faded away, he knelt down with tears flowing from his eyes like a waterfall.
"Motherf*cker, I will kill you all!" He screamed at the top of his lungs and started hammering his fists on the ground in anger. Because before dying, he saw Cynesuke taking her last breath.
He didn't stop until he nearly broke the bones in his hands, before slowly getting up. He looked left and right with bloodshot eyes and started walking randomly.

It was unknown how he was walking, but he suddenly saw an empty lion's nest. He walked into it and found that behind the nest, near the wall, there was a dark hole barely big enough for one person to go inside.

Merlin, being too familiar with this kind of situation of finding hidden secret locations out of nowhere, didn't hesitate for a second and jumped into it, without caring if it was a dead end and he was stuck in a narrow hole, with no place to move or get out.
However, with the world's will backing him and providing an unlimited luck buff, he didn't end up in a hell hole and fell into a small pond.

There was a shiny crystal above the ceiling of the cave, illuminating this small space under the ground. There wasn't much to see, except a small pond, a narrow cave leading God knows where, and a shiny, rockish, basketball-sized, egg-like object at the bottom of the pond.

Merlin, after observing his surroundings with emotionless eyes, picked up the egg-shaped rock and walked out of the small pond. He looked left and right, and after making sure he didn't miss anything, he walked into the narrow cave.

It was unknown how long he had been in this dark, narrow path, but when Merlin walked out from it, he was in a forest and saw the moon right above his head. Obviously, he had been wandering in the dungeon for an entire day. After taking a look at the secret exit of the dungeon, Merlin hugged the egg tightly and walked in the direction of the capital city without saying anything, but the fire of revenge in his eyes was so intense that it wouldn't be long before many people would burn to death under it.

Because he had a skill that made him immortal, he was always very careless about injuries and didn't carry anything on him, just casually throwing some potions in his storage pouch, which he was now regretting.
If he had known about it earlier, he would definitely have carried some healing potions in his pocket.

To make matters worse, Merlin, who was barely running to the teleportation crystal, wanting to leave the dungeon, suddenly heard a loud metal object moving sound, and the shining blue crystal before him also turned grey, obviously becoming offline.
"You've got to be kidding me."
He said with a depressed expression as he turned back and saw a giant hexagram magic array appear in the middle of the boss room, and the entrance door had also closed tightly.
With an eye-blinding white light, a giant white bee, 5 meters in size, appeared in the room, staring at Merlin with a not-so-friendly expression.

Although usually after defeating a boss monster in a dungeon, it doesn't respawn anytime soon, but because this is a new dungeon and mana density in lower floors is many times higher than above, and it had been nearly an hour since the boss was defeated, and to rub salt on Merlin's injuries, it had respawned again at a critical moment, sealing his hope of rescuing his dear pet.
"AHHHH!!!"
Ten minutes later, Merlin again teleported to a random corner of the dungeon, this time on the B1 floor.
Although physically he was completely fine and at full health, there was no longer any light of hope in his eyes.
After the pain of being stomach-pierced by a giant sting faded away, he knelt down with tears flowing from his eyes like a waterfall.
"Motherf*cker, I will kill you all!" He screamed at the top of his lungs and started hammering his fists on the ground in anger.
Because before dying, he saw Cynesuke taking her last breath.
He didn't stop until he nearly broke the bones in his hands, before slowly getting up.
He looked left and right with bloodshot eyes and started walking randomly.
It was unknown how he was walking, but he suddenly saw an empty lion's nest.
He walked into it and found that behind the nest, near the wall, there was a dark hole barely big enough for one person to go inside.

Merlin, being too familiar with this kind of situation of finding hidden secret locations out of nowhere, didn't hesitate for a second and jumped into it, without caring if it was a dead end and he was stuck in a narrow hole, with no place to move or get out.
However, with the world's will backing him and providing an unlimited luck buff, he didn't end up in a hell hole and fell into a small pond.
There was a shiny crystal above the ceiling of the cave, illuminating this small space under the ground.
There wasn't much to see, except a small pond, a narrow cave leading God knows where, and a shiny, rockish, basketball-sized, egg-like object at the bottom of the pond.
Merlin, after observing his surroundings with emotionless eyes, picked up the egg-shaped rock and walked out of the small pond.
He looked left and right, and after making sure he didn't miss anything, he walked into the narrow cave.
It was unknown how long he had been in this dark, narrow path, but when Merlin walked out from it, he was in a forest and saw the moon right above his head.
Obviously, he had been wandering in the dungeon for an entire day.

After taking a look at the secret exit of the dungeon, Merlin hugged the egg tightly and walked in the direction of the capital city without saying anything, but the fire of revenge in his eyes was so intense that it wouldn't be long before many people would burn to death under it.

chapters.title: Chapter 755 - 755. The Endless Maze of Floor B3
paragraphs: "What's wrong with this floor? The change is so big, as if we've come to a completely new dungeon."
When Sylphy arrived on floor B3 and her eyes regained sight, she immediately raised her voice.
It couldn't be helped, as everyone had the same thoughts as her.
The structural layout of floor B3 was something no one had seen before when exploring a dungeon.
The moment they descended to this floor, they saw a 5-square-meter room. And all four corners had doors.

Then, when you opened one of the doors, what lay before it was yet another 5-square-meter room. Inside that room, there were four more doors. Obviously, this time they were stuck in a real high-end maze.
Seeing this kind of troublesome trap, it was indeed reasonable for Sylphy to cry out in anger.

"I hate these types of floors the most," Aisha, beside Myne, started cursing in a low voice. Usually, she didn't lose her temper over such things, as there were many things or people around to make her angry, but this time, she also couldn't control herself.
"Waffle, can you sense mana inside this floor? What's the situation? Can you locate the right path?"
As if predicting he would say that, Waffle immediately raised his head high and sniffed around for mana.
"Mana density here is quite good, but... for some reason, I can't figure out the route leading to the boss room. Something is blocking my senses."

"Maybe it's some kind of security measure of this floor to stop cheaters like us. After all, someone went to great lengths to build such a complicated maze; it would be a pity if someone ruined the other party's effort because they had a special way to find the real route."
Aisha, after hearing Waffle's words, spoke with a thoughtful look. Among all the people and pets in their group, she was the one with the most experience regarding dungeons and their mechanisms.
"Well, if that's the case, then let's go with the original plan and quickly clear this area," Shaking his head, Myne was about to walk forward when Aisha stopped him.

"Wait a minute, idiot. If we walk around this floor mindlessly, I'm sure we'll get lost eventually. I've heard rumours when I was still an adventurer, and that the rooms don't connect together in a straight line like how you perceive them. The real route would most likely be zig-zag, or circular, or something like that."

"Just now, Waffle was unable to figure out the direction, right? What I speculate is that the four doors we're looking at right now, if we do not choose the correct door, I think we will be transported back to the same area again, and stuck in some kind of loop. This was the mechanism I've heard of from adventurers."

"Should we put a landmark for each area? Then even if we get stuck in a loop, we don't have to take the same path again and again," Myne thought a bit and spoke with some uncertainty. He didn't know if this trick was going to work or not. This floor of the dungeon seemed a hard nut to crack.
Hearing Myne's words, Aisha fell into deep thought, and after a minute or so, she came up with a quick plan.

First, Myne and Waffle would go ahead first. This was to check whether they would return to the same area or not. So if they met up with Aisha and the rest, who were waiting at the same spot, then Aisha's theory of opening the correct door was right.

Then, another situation occurred whereby they did not meet up with them even after proceeding forward and got lost in this weird maze. Then Myne could use his teleportation skill to return to the floor entrance, and they could make another plan.
"This certainly is a good idea, but what if my teleportation skill didn't work? This floor doesn't look normal. Don't you guys think we're stuck here?" Myne asked with concern.
"Cough, cough... Myne, I think you should care about yourself more than us," Sylphy interrupted Aisha, who was about to give Myne a 'love fist,' and pointed at the glowing crystal behind her.
"We can leave the dungeon whenever we want, but if you get stuck in the maze, it's hard to say about you, so you care about yourself more than us."

Hearing Sylphy's shameless words, Myne for a moment felt like he was surrounded by traitors who wanted to take his life. Otherwise, whose wives are so cruel that they didn't hesitate to sacrifice their own one and only husband?
"Whose side are you guys on? One day, when I really disappear, only then will you realise my importance..."
Bang!
"Ouch!"

"Bastard, you've disappeared God knows how many times without telling us! We've long ago experienced the feeling of being widows at an early age... Now stop messing around and move your ass. We don't have all day to waste!"

Aisha hit Myne's head irritably, interrupting his nonsense. There was so much work to do at the clan; if she had known that this simple exploration would be so troublesome, she would never have come here.

Today was the first day of their business; it was truly unlucky to hand everything over to a bunch of noobs who didn't understand anything. Now, Aisha felt that if they continued to be so careless, the future of their clan was not very promising.

"Fine, fine. Also, Waffle, you don't have to come with me. I alone will be able to move faster," Saying that, Myne start stretching his muscles as if he is about to run merathon, but corner of his eyes he was looking at Aisha, and when she wasn't paying attention, he quickly pinch her buttock hard, taking revenge for her hitting him twice, and ran away without giving her a chance to fight back.
"Idiot, where can you run? At the end of the day, you will come back to me," Aisha spoke, gritting her teeth, while rubbing her buttock, which was hurting like hell, because Myne used too much force.
Sylphy, Waffle, and Ted, looking at Aisha, whose eyes were about to spit fire, could only shake their heads. They could already imagine Myne's miserable state after he fell into her hands.

After entering the first room, Myne, out of curiosity or maybe to prove Aisha wrong and make fun of her, went straight without any stop. To leave a mark, Myne, who didn't lack mana, at least for the time being, directly summoned a random big rock the size of an adult with the help of his skill, Unique Magic・Sublime Obscurity, which can summon or even create anything out of thin air he wants, as long as he has sufficient mana. This way, even if he is blind, he can't miss such an obvious sign.
Right, right, left, right, left, right, left, right... was the pattern he followed when choosing which doors to open. Anyway, no matter which way he went, everything looked the same.

Then, after going through 10 rooms, he, like previously, continued to rush forward, but seeing Aisha and the others sitting on the floor casually while talking and laughing as if they were on a picnic, the corner of his mouth couldn't help but twist.

"Yo, Myne, you're back... Want to eat something?" Aisha, seeing Myne rushing out from the maze as if someone was chasing him, instantly understood that her prediction was right, and this floor was some kind of loop maze, very difficult to crack.

"You eat yourself! I still have to work, otherwise, you two will definitely drag me into this mess again tomorrow," Myne gave Aisha the middle finger while the others weren't paying attention, since he know very well why she was being so nice, and inviting him to eat, making her raise her eyebrow irritedly, she didn't expected that he would see though her plan.
Then Myne again rushed into the same-looking room with four doors.

"By the way, if this entire floor is a loop maze, then why didn't we encounter Merlin's friends? Aren't they just a little ahead of us? With Myne's speed of running, they should have already encountered him, right?" Sylphy, who remembered that there was also a group of people whom she wanted to beat with them in the dungeon, couldn't help but ask Aisha.

"Maybe after barely defeating the previous boss by sacrificing their so-called friend, they realised that they were overestimating their strength and had left the dungeon instead of continuing forward and risking their lives. After all, it is indeed very profitable to explore an unknown dungeon, but they have to be alive to enjoy the benefits they gain from the dungeon," Aisha thought for a moment and replied while rubbing her chin.

Although most adventurers are very reckless and play with fire all the time, this doesn't mean that they are fools and throw away their lives despite knowing that they are going to lose. Rather, they are more insightful and smart when it comes to saving their lives.

After running into the endless rooms with four doors for half an hour like a mad dog, and dumping nearly 87 big rocks as marks, and ending up meeting his gang around 5 times in this entire process, Myne finally encountered something different.

chapters.title: Chapter 756 - 756. Blood Trails
paragraphs: "Is this the end?"

The room gave Myne a familiar feeling, much like the other small rooms he had been in, but this one was significantly larger. It was a rectangular room, about 15 to 20 meters long, with statues of demons installed in all four corners. In the middle of the room, a huge circle was drawn on the floor.
Myne cautiously placed one foot on the edge of the circle, wondering which evil cult would show their artistic talent in this unknown dungeon. To his surprise, nothing happened.

"Well, it seems like a false alarm," Myne muttered, raising an eyebrow. "Then it shouldn't be a problem to walk forward, but those statues are giving me a bad feeling." He slowly walked toward the centre of the circle.
One step, two steps... then three steps.
As he reached the centre of the circle, the atmosphere in the room changed. The demonic statues in the corners of the room began to move.
[ Name: Gargoyle
LV: 73
Race: Undead Race (Faithfulness Family)
Gender: None
[Skill]
Unique Magic・Thunder
[Ability]
Sharp Fangs and Claws ]

"Stone statues having thunder magic? What kind of logic is this?" Myne's eyes twisted in disbelief. "It doesn't make sense. Shouldn't they have earth magic or summoning magic?" He had seen enough skills and had long ago realised how bizarre many creature skill sets could be. Most of them didn't make sense, but they existed.

"But why are those gargoyles here at all? Are they bosses of this floor or just random mobs? Unique magic for mobs seems a bit too much. By the way, I wonder what the difference is between their thunder and my lightning magic."
Myne watched as the gargoyles turned their heads toward him, their eyes shining with an evil red glint. He muttered to himself before skillfully stealing a skill from a random, unlucky gargoyle.

The gargoyles had dog-like faces with long, pointed teeth and sharp, extended nails. Huge wings grew on their backs, and their entire bodies were made of stone. While Myne was busy stealing their skills, they also flapped their wings and flew into the air, ready to take action and deal with the uninvited guest who had disturbed their sweet sleep.

Just as Myne was wondering why the gargoyles weren't rushing forward and were just flying in the air without doing anything, he suddenly felt a gust of wind pass by him. But that was all. Nothing else happened, leaving him and the gargoyles in confusion.

"Did they just attack me?" Myne realised that the entire room was deep underground, and there was no way a sudden gust of wind could just come and go. It didn't take long for him to figure out that the gargoyles had already started playing their tricks. What he didn't understand was what they had done and why it had no effect on him.

"Maybe they are too weak?" Myne looked at his own level, which was close to 150. With the extra enhancement he got from the gaming world, it would be a miracle if low-level mobs like these gargoyles could even scratch him, let alone give him a decent fight.

The gargoyles saw that their racial skill, Demon Eyes of Fear, which could make their prey fall into a panic and have a chance to be stunned for several tens of seconds, was not taking effect on Myne, even though all four of them were using it together to significantly increase its power. They looked at each other, realising that this opponent was not simple. They nodded and rushed forward, ready to use their ultimate weapon after getting close to Myne.

But to their surprise, after they got close to Myne, they couldn't use their Unique Magic Thunder, no matter how hard they tried. Instead, Myne gave them a mocking smile. The next moment, under their horrified gaze, Myne's entire body was surrounded by blue thunder.

His hair stood on end, his eyes turned blue with lightning flashing in them, and with a loud thunderous boom, a white light covered the entire room. A giant explosion, full of thunder and lightning, spread everywhere from his body, destroying everything in its path.
Upon Myne regaining his vision, the dust settled to reveal him standing in the middle of a two-meter-deep crater with no gargoyles in sight.

"Well, I overdid it this time. It's felt like using a giant fireball to kill a mosquito," Myne chuckled to himself. "And people say gargoyles are immune to magic attacks. It's not that they're immune; it's just that the people attacking them are too weak to break through their defences."
Shaking his head, Myne walked out of the crater, ready to move forward.

"Hmm? What's this?" Myne's eyes landed on a spherical stone on the ground that emitted a large amount of magic. He picked it up with deep interest and used his appraisal skill on it, realising it was a Gargoyle's core. Undead stone creatures like gargoyles and golems all have a magic core that acts as their heart and the source of their magic.

"If I were a poor adventurer, this would be a nice loot," Myne said with a lack of interest, but he still threw the core in his hand and the remaining three on the ground into his inventory. He decided to give them to Aisha and Sylphy as a gift. After all, this was their clan's first mission, and it would be good to collect some souvenirs.

"Now, where to go next?" Myne looked around but couldn't find any other doors or teleportation crystals to move deeper into the dungeon. He used some of his skills, but he didn't have any specific skill for investigation, and the dungeon itself was a bit weird. Even if he did have such a skill, it probably wouldn't work.

"Forget it. It's better to leave this kind of brain-burning work to the girls," Shaking his head, Myne opened a portal in front of him and waited for a few seconds before Aisha and the others walked out.

"So, you finally found the end of the maze. Nice, I'm proud of you," Aisha said, rubbing Myne's hair and treating him like a child. Myne gave her a cold look, but she didn't care and instead looked at the room, which appeared as if someone had thrown a giant bomb in it.
"Just what kind of enemy were you facing that you caused so much destruction?" Sylphy asked with a frown.
"Gargoyles. Impressed?" Myne replied with a hint of pride in his voice, obviously very satisfied with his explosive art.

"Huh? For a second, I thought you fought dragons. Did you have to go this far just to deal with a few gargoyles?" Sylphy gave Myne a speechless look, as if she were looking at a prodigal who didn't care about wasting mana at all.
"Myne, there seems to be a door over there!"
Myne followed Waffle's pointed direction, but there was nothing. Confused, he went near the wall, and suddenly a door appeared out of nowhere.

"A hidden passage! So that is the way to move forward. Thankfully, we have Waffle; otherwise, it would have been hard to find it," Aisha said, feeling relieved and praising Waffle, which made him immensely proud.
"Myne, look over here!" Just then, they heard Sylphy's high-pitched voice. What she had found was a tremendously large pool of blood spreading all over the floor.
"And there are traces of something being dragged into the darkness."
"This is a lot of blood. It's not from a single person. There were several... no, a considerable number of people."
As they got near the blood, everyone's nose caught a rusty iron smell mixed in with the blood.
"Myne, this blood is still warm!" Ted, who had the strongest nose among them, spoke with a frown and looked at the darkness ahead.
"Do you think the people who came ahead of us haven't left yet and are still inside?" Sylphy asked worriedly.

"Is there even a need to ask? Obviously, those guys are still playing hide-and-seek with us. I wonder what's wrong with their brains. Is money more important than their lives?" Aisha shook her head. "Despite knowing that they are no match for the monsters deep in the dungeon, they still insist on challenging them. This is simply a suicide attempt."

"Let's go. We can ask them personally what's wrong with their brains if they're still alive." Myne didn't have as many thoughts as his wives. He simply looked at the blood before continuing to walk forward, not caring whether some random cannon fodder lived or died.
As they followed the traces of blood that were dragged along, they found stairs that continued down into the depths of the floor.

But to their surprise, after they got close to Myne, they couldn't use their Unique Magic Thunder, no matter how hard they tried.
Instead, Myne gave them a mocking smile.
The next moment, under their horrified gaze, Myne's entire body was surrounded by blue thunder.
His hair stood on end, his eyes turned blue with lightning flashing in them, and with a loud thunderous boom, a white light covered the entire room.
A giant explosion, full of thunder and lightning, spread everywhere from his body, destroying everything in its path.
Upon Myne regaining his vision, the dust settled to reveal him standing in the middle of a two-meter-deep crater with no gargoyles in sight.
"Well, I overdid it this time.
It's felt like using a giant fireball to kill a mosquito," Myne chuckled to himself.
"And people say gargoyles are immune to magic attacks.
It's not that they're immune; it's just that the people attacking them are too weak to break through their defences."
Shaking his head, Myne walked out of the crater, ready to move forward.
"Hmm?
What's this?" Myne's eyes landed on a spherical stone on the ground that emitted a large amount of magic.
He picked it up with deep interest and used his appraisal skill on it, realising it was a Gargoyle's core.
Undead stone creatures like gargoyles and golems all have a magic core that acts as their heart and the source of their magic.
"If I were a poor adventurer, this would be a nice loot," Myne said with a lack of interest, but he still threw the core in his hand and the remaining three on the ground into his inventory.
He decided to give them to Aisha and Sylphy as a gift.
After all, this was their clan's first mission, and it would be good to collect some souvenirs.
"Now, where to go next?" Myne looked around but couldn't find any other doors or teleportation crystals to move deeper into the dungeon.
He used some of his skills, but he didn't have any specific skill for investigation, and the dungeon itself was a bit weird.
Even if he did have such a skill, it probably wouldn't work.
"Forget it.
It's better to leave this kind of brain-burning work to the girls," Shaking his head, Myne opened a portal in front of him and waited for a few seconds before Aisha and the others walked out.
"So, you finally found the end of the maze.
Nice, I'm proud of you," Aisha said, rubbing Myne's hair and treating him like a child.
Myne gave her a cold look, but she didn't care and instead looked at the room, which appeared as if someone had thrown a giant bomb in it.
"Just what kind of enemy were you facing that you caused so much destruction?" Sylphy asked with a frown.
"Gargoyles.
Impressed?" Myne replied with a hint of pride in his voice, obviously very satisfied with his explosive art.
"Huh?
For a second, I thought you fought dragons.
Did you have to go this far just to deal with a few gargoyles?" Sylphy gave Myne a speechless look, as if she were looking at a prodigal who didn't care about wasting mana at all.
"Myne, there seems to be a door over there!"
Myne followed Waffle's pointed direction, but there was nothing.
Confused, he went near the wall, and suddenly a door appeared out of nowhere.
"A hidden passage!
So that is the way to move forward.
Thankfully, we have Waffle; otherwise, it would have been hard to find it," Aisha said, feeling relieved and praising Waffle, which made him immensely proud.
"Myne, look over here!" Just then, they heard Sylphy's high-pitched voice.
What she had found was a tremendously large pool of blood spreading all over the floor.
"And there are traces of something being dragged into the darkness."
"This is a lot of blood.
It's not from a single person.
There were several... no, a considerable number of people."
As they got near the blood, everyone's nose caught a rusty iron smell mixed in with the blood.
"Myne, this blood is still warm!" Ted, who had the strongest nose among them, spoke with a frown and looked at the darkness ahead.
"Do you think the people who came ahead of us haven't left yet and are still inside?" Sylphy asked worriedly.
"Is there even a need to ask?
Obviously, those guys are still playing hide-and-seek with us.
I wonder what's wrong with their brains.
Is money more important than their lives?" Aisha shook her head.
"Despite knowing that they are no match for the monsters deep in the dungeon, they still insist on challenging them.
This is simply a suicide attempt."
"Let's go.
We can ask them personally what's wrong with their brains if they're still alive." Myne didn't have as many thoughts as his wives.
He simply looked at the blood before continuing to walk forward, not caring whether some random cannon fodder lived or died.
As they followed the traces of blood that were dragged along, they found stairs that continued down into the depths of the floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 757 - 757. A Gentleman
paragraphs: "Should we go?" Sylphy asked nervously, seeing the bloody trail continue down the staircase. She was obviously not fond of the dark passage leading into deeper darkness.
"Otherwise, do you plan to stand here? Don't you want to go home? The faster we deal with this shit, the faster we can go back," Myne put his arm around Sylphy and led her down the staircase.

"Should we use something to light up? It's a bit too dark here; I can barely see anything," Aisha asked. Her suggestion was refused by Myne, who, after getting the Nightwalker's bloodline, could see in the darkness as clearly as in the daytime.

He didn't want to attract random monsters by illuminating the surroundings and becoming a target. Since he was powerful enough to handle anything, his vision was more than enough to ensure everyone's safety, so they just had to follow him and leave the rest to him.

"Is this the fourth basement floor? So far, I have never seen such structures in any of the other dungeons I've been to," Sylphy said with a frown, looking at the pitch black darkness around her, giving her a very creepy vibe.

"Neither have I. Is this some kind of hidden place? Otherwise, there's no explanation for why we're here. We should have gone directly to the boss room or a teleportation point to move to the next floor or get out of the dungeon," Aisha said, looking around while explaining.

Unlike the previous floor, this time a vast scene lay before them, so vast that even the endpoint couldn't be seen. There was only one straight line, going from one end to the other. The only thing that existed on this floor was this passageway. There was nothing else.

"Maybe it's another maze-type trap. There should be a hidden door somewhere on this floor, similar to how we found the door on the third basement floor. We can only move forward after finding it. This is going to be a pain in the ass again," Myne said, annoyed, while rubbing his forehead.
He quickly wanted to complete this mission and go back home so he could enter the gaming world and visit Cosmic Arena or play another dungeon, but now he was stuck in this never-ending dungeon.

"By the way, the blood trail continues deep into this passage. Do you think someone deliberately left this so we, like idiots, would follow it and jump into another party's trap?" Myne, who was the only one who could see crystal-clearly, spoke while taking out a magic lamp and illuminating the surroundings.

Since there was only a single passage on this floor, he didn't have to worry about a sneak attack. As long as he walked in front, everything would be fine, so there was no need to let everyone continue to be blind. God knows if he missed the hidden door because of overconfidence, and since the others couldn't see in the darkness, wouldn't they be stuck on this floor?
"Finally, some light. Now I feel much better," Sylphy breathed a sigh of relief as she was able to see again.
"Wow, that's a lot of blood. I don't think the person who lost so much blood would be able to see tomorrow's sun," Aisha said, kneeling down to observe the bloodstain before shaking her head.

If not for the fact that everyone in her team was very powerful and she knew Myne could teleport them out if things went wrong, she would have long ago fled from this dungeon just by seeing all those creepy things along the way. She cared about her life more than some illusory reputation.
"Let's move on; there's no need to waste more time," Myne said, leading everyone into the dark, creepy passage that looked like it was leading them to the abyss.
Thud!

"What was that?" Suddenly hearing a noise out of thin air, Myne and the others, who had long ago lost their vigilance after walking for forty minutes without finding anything, jolted awake. They began looking ahead with focus while taking a defensive stance.
"Myne, I think there's something ahead," Waffle said, narrowing his eyes and speaking seriously.

"I can see that," Myne didn't take the thing in front of him seriously because, in his eyes, whatever was ahead was just small fry that could be dealt with easily; there was no need to make a mountain out of a molehill.
"Gurururururuuuu!"
"So...meone...sa...ve...me"
"Ah, I see it. It's a Chimera. No wonder it was making so many weird noises; for once, I thought there were a lot of monsters ahead."

Race: Magic Creature ( Experimental Body ) ( Faithfulness and Mythical Beast )
Gender: None
[Skill]
Unique Magic ・ Aurora
Unique Magic ・ Storm
Demon Eyes of Deadly Poison
[Ability]
Chewing
Iron Bite
Poisonous Fang
Fast Flight
Tackle
Rock Skin
Roar
Super Speed
Poison Needle
Fast Learner
High Endurance
Water Breathing
Faster Swimmer
Iron Tail
Night Vision
Minor Healing ]

F*ck! So many abilities. It's my first time seeing someone with more than three abilities. Even divine beasts don't have this kind of privilege. This motherf*cker definitely has some unspoken relationship with Lady Luck. Myne's eyes widened in shock as he looked at the Chimera's status.

But come to think of it, I shouldn't be so surprised, after all, this creature is a super hybrid of who knows how many different beasts, so it's bound to gain some of their abilities. And it also has an 'Experimental Body' tag, which means someone has messed with its already messy body, giving it even more weird abilities." Myne mused, rubbing his chin.
"Myne! Over there!" Aisha suddenly shouted, pointing at the Chimera's mouth. Myne looked and saw it eating someone's arm.
They heard a voice coming from under the Chimera. It seemed to have been saving food for later instead of finishing everyone immediately.

Myne looked closer and saw a middle-aged man with thinning hair lying beneath the creature. His right arm and left foot were torn off, and his entire body was covered in blood. Only God knew how he was still alive after sustaining such large, deadly injuries and losing a huge amount of blood.

"Hey, you guys there, I can see you... Are you the ones who defeated those Gargoyles? Can you please save me? I'm willing to give you anything. Please save me, I don't want to die. My wife and seven children are waiting for me at home..."

"How is he able to speak so calmly?" Sylphy wondered, becoming wary. "Isn't he feeling any pain? That Chimera looks very heavy. If it sat on me, I wouldn't be able to breathe properly, let alone pretend to be calm and act as if I'm just asking for a glass of water."

"Then should I just blast both of them and clear the way? It seems pointless to help him and waste our time, Myne asked, not having the same thoughts as Sylphy. To him, every strange event could be explained with one word: "Skills." There were so many weird skills out there that it was no surprise this guy could still be at ease despite losing half his body.

"Don't be so cold-blooded, Myne. We need this guy to know what's going on with him and his friends, whether they left the dungeon or are still wandering around, and most importantly, how they found this dungeon."

"Fine, fine, you're the boss," Myne said, rolling his eyes as if he didn't expect such an answer from her. He walked forward, ready to send the Chimera on its way and, of course, steal its two juicy unique skills. He hadn't expected to be so lucky as to get three unique skills in a single day.

But he had only taken a few steps when a man with long black hair, pale white skin, and crimson eyes, wearing a red tuxedo, emerged from the darkness. The most unusual thing about him was the two hard, pointy horns on his head. He stood beside the Chimera, which now looked nothing like a mystical beast but more like a pet dog, caring only about the food in its mouth and ignoring everything else as if it were invisible.
"Hello, everyone. How may I help you?" The horned man spoke with a smile, his hands behind his back like a gentleman.

"Are you a demon?" Myne asked, looking at the horns. But the man's modern clothing style made it difficult for him to relate this guy to the demons he had heard about in stories, who were nothing but barbaric killers.

"Ah, it's as you guessed. I'm one of the random guys from the Demon race. The name's Xanadu. Nice to meet you," The horned man turned out to be surprisingly polite, completely dumbfounding everyone on Myne's team.
"I'd like you to hand that person over there to us. We have some questions to ask him," Myne, although shocked, quickly returned to business.

"Hahaha, you seem to be quite a rude person, huh? Even though I've given you my name, where are your manners, young man?" The horned man said with a faint smile, seeming to be in a good mood and not minding wasting time.
"When did demons start having a sense of courtesy?" Myne rubbed his head in confusion and looked back at his wives, who were also dumbfounded, not knowing what to do.

"Forget it. My name is Myne, and now give that idiot to us." Myne shrugged and waved his hand. As for apologising, there was no way he was going to do that; it wasn't like he had asked for the other party's name in the first place.
