chapters.title: Chapter 758 - 758. Enemies by Nature
paragraphs: "There's nothing better I can expect from a human. You're all the same; you have no patience or respect for others at all."

With a smile still on his face, Xanadu shook his head and spoke softly. He wasn't surprised that Myne was rude to him. After all, their races were eternal enemies. How could they act like friends when they met? It was already a good thing they hadn't started fighting.

Because Xanadu wasn't pleased with Myne's answer, he looked at the middle-aged man who was getting eaten alive by his pet chimera and kicked him in the stomach, making him spit out a mouthful of blood.
Myne raised an eyebrow, seeing the demon hit the middle-aged man while ignoring his request.
"Since you don't want to hand him over, there's nothing more to say," Myne said, moving forward as a giant fireball began forming in his palm.

At first, Xanadu looked at Myne's action with a playful expression, thinking the other party was taking him a bit too lightly. But as the fireball continued to grow, the calmness on his face began to fade.
"Test Subject Number 1, you've eaten so much already. I'm sure your stomach is full now, right? Would you mind not eating this one and giving it to me instead?"
"Guooooo..."
Hearing Xanadu's words, the chimera growled unhappily. It first looked at the miserable middle-aged man, then at Myne, who held a dangerous, super-giant fireball above his palm.
The fireball was twice the size of the chimera's own height, and Myne's cold eyes were staring at him, ready to send him to his ancestor.

After a moment of silence, the chimera got up, walked a short distance away, and sat down to chew on the arm in its mouth, not caring about anything else. Everyone here looked very dangerous, and as a smart monster, it didn't want to die young.

"How was it? It seems like he won't be eating your friend anymore. Let me give this person back to you in honour of your polite attitude," Xanadu said, grabbing the middle-aged man by the neck and throwing him to Myne, who slowly let the fireball dissipate.

"'Polite attitude' my ass. If I wasn't powerful enough to threaten you, only God knows if we'd still be talking," Myne said, bluntly exposing Xanadu's nonsense. He didn't care about Xanadu's feelings. He lifted the middle-aged man, who seemed to want to say something, and threw him to Aisha.
"Ow... it... hurts..."

The middle-aged man's wounds, barely sealed by his magical artefacts, had allowed him to live this long. After being tossed around twice, all his wounds opened again, and blood began gushing out like a fountain, making his already pale face even paler. It looked like he could die at any moment.
Aisha quickly rushed to the man and used her healing skills to stabilise his wounds and stop the bleeding.

Thankfully, whatever magical artefact he had seemed to still be working, and the bleeding soon stopped. Otherwise, with just Aisha's low-level healing skill, it would have been nearly impossible to save him. After all, the chimera had eaten one of his arms and a leg and taken a large bite out of his waist—more than enough for any normal person to book a permanent ticket to hell. How could he still have time to ask for help?
"Well then, is that fine with you? Do you need anything else?" Xanadu asked with a smile. After Aisha finished healing the middle-aged man, he stopped staring at her and turned back to Myne.

"No, that's all," Myne replied with a cold, impatient face. He wanted to end this mission quickly, but things were getting more and more complicated, making him lose his composure. And now, this good-for-nothing demon was trying to act like a gentleman by blocking his way and not helping with anything.
Motherf*cker, just go your own way. We have work to do, Myne thought, and he was about to shoo Xanadu away, but Xanadu began to speak before him.

"You and your team, what can I say? You're not the norm that I know. Most of the humans I know, when they see a demon, either immediately attack us without a word or simply do everything they can to run away. So, this is a valuable experience to have. So, Myne, was it? May I ask why you are in this dungeon? Maybe I can help with something. Nobody knows this dungeon better than I do. You can fully trust in my professionalism."
"We came to crush this goddamn dungeon."

Myne didn't care about Xanadu's feelings, whether he might have wasted a dozen years creating this dungeon or not. This dungeon had tested him a bit too much, and there was no way he was going to let it go. Even if the Demon King himself came here to stop him today, he still wouldn't go home without destroying this dungeon.
Hearing the anger in Myne's answer, Xanadu's right eyebrow flickered slightly. He didn't understand why Myne was so angry with his dungeon.

Did he lose one of his team members here? But none of his team members looks weak. It's impossible for low-level monsters from the upper floors to hurt them. So the reason must be different, Xanadu thought.
"Oh, this dungeon... huh? Do you guys know that we, the Demon race, were the ones who created these dungeons?"

"Yes, but as far as I remember, dungeons can also be created naturally, so you can't take all the credit." Without any hesitation, Myne rubbed salt in Xanadu's old wounds. This is why demons and humans can hardly tolerate each other. They're like a couple who have ended their honeymoon period and are now fighting over every little thing.

"Yes, what you said is right, but do you have any idea how rare natural dungeons are? Out of the hundreds of thousands of dungeons out there, barely one percent are natural, while the rest—ninety-nine percent—were created by demons. Which means, by destroying this dungeon, you are declaring that you and I are enemies. Is that what you are saying?" Suddenly, Xanadu's aura changed, and he exuded a very oppressive feeling.

"Ohoho, I'm sure that's what it will lead to, and believe me, you are now behaving normally. As a demon, this is how you should be." An excited, wide grin appeared on Myne's face. Finally, he didn't have to talk nonsense and could get some action.
"Uhahahahahahaha. You have indeed piqued my interest."
Bang!

"Can't you wait until I've finished speaking?" Xanadu looked at Myne helplessly as a dozen or so wind blades shot past him, landing on his iron-like body without leaving any damage. Still, it interrupted his speech.

"I'm tired of your nonsense. Either you start fighting, or you just get the hell out of my way. You are just wasting my precious time," Myne, who was already very impatient, saw that Xanadu had no intention of taking action and was just teasing him.

He lost his calm and shot a dozen wind blades to make him angry, so that he would attack. He wanted to clear the way in one fell swoop; after all, his wives were watching him. He couldn't just slap a smiling person, right?
"Pillows, come here," Xanadu didn't take his eyes off Myne, fearing that the other party would throw another attack, and called out to someone.
"Pillows? What kind of name is that?"

While Myne and his teammates were wondering what kind of creature had that name, a pretty figure suddenly walked out from behind the Chimera. She was about thirty years old, with dark skin, long raven hair, black eyes, an hourglass-shaped body, and F-cup-sized breasts. She wore revealing black leather armour and a short skirt that fully highlighted her breathtaking figure, enough to make Myne's heart beat faster.

Damn, how can this demon have such a hot subordinate? And is she an elf? As Myne was staring at Pillows's sexy figure, he suddenly noticed her unusually long, pointy ears, which looked exactly the same as Amy's.

"You guys seem very surprised to see her. Let me introduce you: this is my cute little subordinate. Her name is Pillows. It's as you see—she is an elf... but she's not your usual elf who has white skin and golden hair. She is a subspecies of elf, a dark elf," Xanadu introduced the dark elf, Pillows, to Myne and the others with a playful smile.

The hot dark elf named Pillows was throwing hateful glances at Myne and the others. Obviously, like other elves, she didn't have a good impression of humans, which is normal since they are in high demand among humans, and naturally, she would be hunted down if she were seen within any human city, leaving her no place to go except to demons.

"Hello there, nice to meet you. By the way, have we met before?" Myne, who always had a special place for beautiful and rare women in his heart, instantly put on his "good guy" mask and politely greeted Pillows. Sadly, she wasn't interested in a random human "nobody" and just turned her face away with disgust.
"Hehehe... This girl has an extreme hatred toward Humans, so please don't mind her being mean. Well, I'll leave it to your imagination as to why she hates humans."
"Well, Myne, while we're at it, shall we play a game? You're definitely going to like it."

sentences.text: "There's nothing better I can expect from a human.
You're all the same; you have no patience or respect for others at all."
With a smile still on his face, Xanadu shook his head and spoke softly.
He wasn't surprised that Myne was rude to him.
After all, their races were eternal enemies.
How could they act like friends when they met?
It was already a good thing they hadn't started fighting.

Because Xanadu wasn't pleased with Myne's answer, he looked at the middle-aged man who was getting eaten alive by his pet chimera and kicked him in the stomach, making him spit out a mouthful of blood.
Myne raised an eyebrow, seeing the demon hit the middle-aged man while ignoring his request.
"Since you don't want to hand him over, there's nothing more to say," Myne said, moving forward as a giant fireball began forming in his palm.
At first, Xanadu looked at Myne's action with a playful expression, thinking the other party was taking him a bit too lightly.
But as the fireball continued to grow, the calmness on his face began to fade.
"Test Subject Number 1, you've eaten so much already.
I'm sure your stomach is full now, right?
Would you mind not eating this one and giving it to me instead?"
"Guooooo..."
Hearing Xanadu's words, the chimera growled unhappily.
It first looked at the miserable middle-aged man, then at Myne, who held a dangerous, super-giant fireball above his palm.
The fireball was twice the size of the chimera's own height, and Myne's cold eyes were staring at him, ready to send him to his ancestor.
After a moment of silence, the chimera got up, walked a short distance away, and sat down to chew on the arm in its mouth, not caring about anything else.
Everyone here looked very dangerous, and as a smart monster, it didn't want to die young.
"How was it?
It seems like he won't be eating your friend anymore.
Let me give this person back to you in honour of your polite attitude," Xanadu said, grabbing the middle-aged man by the neck and throwing him to Myne, who slowly let the fireball dissipate.
"'Polite attitude' my ass.
If I wasn't powerful enough to threaten you, only God knows if we'd still be talking," Myne said, bluntly exposing Xanadu's nonsense.
He didn't care about Xanadu's feelings.
He lifted the middle-aged man, who seemed to want to say something, and threw him to Aisha.
"Ow... it... hurts..."
The middle-aged man's wounds, barely sealed by his magical artefacts, had allowed him to live this long.
After being tossed around twice, all his wounds opened again, and blood began gushing out like a fountain, making his already pale face even paler.
It looked like he could die at any moment.
Aisha quickly rushed to the man and used her healing skills to stabilise his wounds and stop the bleeding.
Thankfully, whatever magical artefact he had seemed to still be working, and the bleeding soon stopped.
Otherwise, with just Aisha's low-level healing skill, it would have been nearly impossible to save him.
After all, the chimera had eaten one of his arms and a leg and taken a large bite out of his waist—more than enough for any normal person to book a permanent ticket to hell.
How could he still have time to ask for help?
"Well then, is that fine with you?
Do you need anything else?" Xanadu asked with a smile.
After Aisha finished healing the middle-aged man, he stopped staring at her and turned back to Myne.
"No, that's all," Myne replied with a cold, impatient face.
He wanted to end this mission quickly, but things were getting more and more complicated, making him lose his composure.
And now, this good-for-nothing demon was trying to act like a gentleman by blocking his way and not helping with anything.
Motherf*cker, just go your own way.
We have work to do, Myne thought, and he was about to shoo Xanadu away, but Xanadu began to speak before him.
"You and your team, what can I say?
You're not the norm that I know.
Most of the humans I know, when they see a demon, either immediately attack us without a word or simply do everything they can to run away.
So, this is a valuable experience to have.
So, Myne, was it?
May I ask why you are in this dungeon?
Maybe I can help with something.
Nobody knows this dungeon better than I do.
You can fully trust in my professionalism."
"We came to crush this goddamn dungeon."
Myne didn't care about Xanadu's feelings, whether he might have wasted a dozen years creating this dungeon or not.
This dungeon had tested him a bit too much, and there was no way he was going to let it go.
Even if the Demon King himself came here to stop him today, he still wouldn't go home without destroying this dungeon.
Hearing the anger in Myne's answer, Xanadu's right eyebrow flickered slightly.
He didn't understand why Myne was so angry with his dungeon.
Did he lose one of his team members here?
But none of his team members looks weak.
It's impossible for low-level monsters from the upper floors to hurt them.
So the reason must be different, Xanadu thought.
"Oh, this dungeon... huh?
Do you guys know that we, the Demon race, were the ones who created these dungeons?"
"Yes, but as far as I remember, dungeons can also be created naturally, so you can't take all the credit." Without any hesitation, Myne rubbed salt in Xanadu's old wounds.
This is why demons and humans can hardly tolerate each other.
They're like a couple who have ended their honeymoon period and are now fighting over every little thing.
"Yes, what you said is right, but do you have any idea how rare natural dungeons are?
Out of the hundreds of thousands of dungeons out there, barely one percent are natural, while the rest—ninety-nine percent—were created by demons.
Which means, by destroying this dungeon, you are declaring that you and I are enemies.
Is that what you are saying?" Suddenly, Xanadu's aura changed, and he exuded a very oppressive feeling.
"Ohoho, I'm sure that's what it will lead to, and believe me, you are now behaving normally.
As a demon, this is how you should be." An excited, wide grin appeared on Myne's face.
Finally, he didn't have to talk nonsense and could get some action.
"Uhahahahahahaha.
You have indeed piqued my interest."
Bang!
"Can't you wait until I've finished speaking?" Xanadu looked at Myne helplessly as a dozen or so wind blades shot past him, landing on his iron-like body without leaving any damage.
Still, it interrupted his speech.
"I'm tired of your nonsense.
Either you start fighting, or you just get the hell out of my way.
You are just wasting my precious time," Myne, who was already very impatient, saw that Xanadu had no intention of taking action and was just teasing him.
He lost his calm and shot a dozen wind blades to make him angry, so that he would attack.
He wanted to clear the way in one fell swoop; after all, his wives were watching him.
He couldn't just slap a smiling person, right?
"Pillows, come here," Xanadu didn't take his eyes off Myne, fearing that the other party would throw another attack, and called out to someone.
"Pillows?
What kind of name is that?"
While Myne and his teammates were wondering what kind of creature had that name, a pretty figure suddenly walked out from behind the Chimera.
She was about thirty years old, with dark skin, long raven hair, black eyes, an hourglass-shaped body, and F-cup-sized breasts.
She wore revealing black leather armour and a short skirt that fully highlighted her breathtaking figure, enough to make Myne's heart beat faster.
Damn, how can this demon have such a hot subordinate?
And is she an elf?
As Myne was staring at Pillows's sexy figure, he suddenly noticed her unusually long, pointy ears, which looked exactly the same as Amy's.
"You guys seem very surprised to see her.
Let me introduce you: this is my cute little subordinate.
Her name is Pillows.
It's as you see—she is an elf... but she's not your usual elf who has white skin and golden hair.
She is a subspecies of elf, a dark elf," Xanadu introduced the dark elf, Pillows, to Myne and the others with a playful smile.
The hot dark elf named Pillows was throwing hateful glances at Myne and the others.

Obviously, like other elves, she didn't have a good impression of humans, which is normal since they are in high demand among humans, and naturally, she would be hunted down if she were seen within any human city, leaving her no place to go except to demons.
"Hello there, nice to meet you.
By the way, have we met before?" Myne, who always had a special place for beautiful and rare women in his heart, instantly put on his "good guy" mask and politely greeted Pillows.
Sadly, she wasn't interested in a random human "nobody" and just turned her face away with disgust.
"Hehehe...
This girl has an extreme hatred toward Humans, so please don't mind her being mean.
Well, I'll leave it to your imagination as to why she hates humans."
"Well, Myne, while we're at it, shall we play a game?
You're definitely going to like it."

This wasn't the first time Myne had encountered this kind of situation, especially since he started going to Abyssal Paradise ( Gaming World ), so he wasn't surprised at all. He only felt a bit disappointed since he wanted to see the difference between a demon from his world and a real demon from Hell.
"Alright, since you're so excited about this silly game, let's finish it quickly. But I have some conditions," Myne said calmly, making Xanadu raise his eyebrow.
"And what kind of conditions?"
"First of all, Aisha, Sylphy, Waffle, and Ted will be fighting in pairs against your teammates since they have a racial advantage," Myne stated, moving forward.
"Then I'd also like to ask who will be facing me? It seems there are only five of you?" Xanadu also moved forward, asking playfully.
"Don't worry, I am more than enough to deal with you," Myne replied bluntly. He still couldn't understand why this demon was so confident about dealing with him.
"Alright, fair enough. And what is your next condition?"

This time, Myne didn't reply. Instead, he used a telepathy skill on Xanadu, who at first frowned and resisted it, but then, figuring out that Myne was trying to have a private conversation with him, he let him enter his mind.
"Now what are you trying to be so mysterious about that you don't want your teammates to know?" Xanadu spoke playfully.
"I want you to hand over Pillow's slave contract," Myne directly put forward his demand without beating around the bush.
"And what would I get if you lose?" Xanadu asked with a smile, not minding Myne's perverted gaze on his slave.

"I won't kill you, and I'll let you go," Myne answered, confused, since this was all he could think of that might be worth more than anything else. After all, to use anything in the world, you have to be alive.
"Deal. I'm looking forward to fighting you." Xanadu paused for a few seconds, staring at Myne without blinking, before putting on his trademark smile and shaking his hand with him, closing the deal.
After that, Myne returned to Aisha and the others for a small team meeting.
"So what's next?" Aisha asked while crossing her arms below her enormous bosom.
"What else? The same as usual. Go and beat their asses and finish this goddamn mission," Myne said, pretending to be annoyed, and continued.

"I've made a deal with that guy. Waffle and Ted, and you two, will team up in a pair and beat down the Chimera and the elf girl. In the final, I will face that demon. This is the so-called game he wants to play... Sigh, nowadays, demons have no creativity at all. Is this even a game?"

Shaking his head, Myne looked at his group and found that none of them had any problem with his plan and nodded with satisfaction. He first thought they would ask some dumb questions like why they had to fight, but it seemed like they were more mature than he had expected.

"By the way, do we really have to fight with that elf girl? Can't we somehow persuade her to withdraw from the combat and let her join us? You see, there are barely any elves left in the world, and it would be such a shame to let her follow a demon."

"If Amy knew about it, she would be very sad... Also, we need more staff in our clan. Someone as powerful as her would definitely be a great help," Aisha's suggestion caught everyone off guard, but after thinking for a while, everyone found what she said made sense, especially Myne, who was literally laughing to the point of tears in his heart.

He couldn't say how grateful he was for Aisha's kind intention. Now he didn't have to worry about where to place his new 'waifu.' He could let her follow the other girls as a bodyguard and spy, getting all their information, and in his free time, he could also play with her wholeheartedly.
What kind of good karma did I do in my previous life to have such a wonderful wife? Myne couldn't help but give Aisha an unexpected hug and a deep kiss, leaving everyone dumbfounded.
"Why are you so kind?" He said, wiping nonexistent tears from the corner of his eyes before clapping his hands in excitement, interrupting Sylphy, who seemed to want to say something.

"So it's decided, we are going to save that poor child and bring her under our wing. As a lonely elf stuck between those evil demons, we have to save her no matter what." Saying that, Myne paused. He thought for a few seconds before turning back to Aisha.
"How are we going to do that?"

chapters.title: Chapter 760 - 760. Hidden Move
paragraphs: "Well, are you guys done with your preparation? If you intended to kill me with boredom, then you're already halfway to success!" Xanadu, who was nearly out of patience, yelled out, disturbing Myne and the others' meeting.
"Yes, yes, we are done. You demon are so impatient," Myne shook his head and took a couch out of his inventory. He set it down and sat on it while gesturing for Xanadu to start his so-called game.

"Hmph, you certainly have self-confidence, don't you? Alright then, please do your best not to die immediately; otherwise, I'll feel bad for wasting so much time," Xanadu, holding back his anger, gave a forced smile before looking at his pet Chimera, who unwillingly got up and roared loudly.
"Guooooooooo!!"
"Well, your first match will be against Test Subject Number 1, so who among you will go first?"

"Waffle, Ted, if you two lose, you'd better not show me your face for the next entire month, or you won't end up well," Myne gave Waffle and Ted an unfriendly look. Both of them understood that their leisure time was at risk, so they nodded at him with a serious expression before rushing forward.
"Waffuuuu!"
"Wovuuuu!"
"Why are you two making noise pollution like that idiot beast!"

Waffle and Ted hadn't even finished showing off their might like the Chimera before Myne poured cold water on their excitement and interrupted their joy, earning a hateful look from them. But he didn't care about their mood and scowled at them to hurry up.
"We have to teach this bastard a lesson," Waffle spoke to Ted in a low voice, not taking the Chimera coming toward them seriously.

"Yes, recently he's been a bit too much of an asshole with us... Should we disclose his affair with Sylphy's mother? That blow should be enough for him to get beaten to death by Aisha and the others, right?" Ted asked with a sinister smile.

Although Myne always tried to be careful while having fun with Garnet (Sylphy's mother), there was barely a 10-meter distance between her house and his. With Waffle and Ted's monstrous physiques, how could they, who always wandered around the houses looking for fun, never encounter weird noises coming out from Garnet's house and curiously sneak in to look for the source?

They had known for a long time the reason why Garnet had moved near their house and so close to Myne, but because they thought this secret could be used against Myne as an ultimate weapon someday, they never disclosed it and always pretended as if they didn't know anything about it.

"It's a good idea, but we have to be careful. I saw Myne using some kind of weird skill to manipulate June one time, and she did what he told her like a puppet. We'd better not get caught, or our end won't be simple," Waffle reminded Ted with a serious look before throwing hundreds of fire bullets at the Chimera.

Myne, who was watching the battle, feeling a bit bored and occasionally sneaking a peek at Pillow's voluptuous figure while imagining all kinds of moves he was going to play with her, suddenly felt chill run down his spine as if he was being targeted.

"Which bastard is so free to think bad things about me?" Myne looked at Xanadu, but finding that the other party was busy watching the battle and didn't look like anything evil was going on inside his mind for him, he rubbed his hair in confusion, wondering who else could be targeting him.
Never in his dream could he imagine that just because of a few words he said to encourage Waffle and Ted, both of them had already started looking for a place to dig a grave for him.

However, because the film could only block one direction instead of covering the Chimera fully, the gravity effect on it didn't disappear, and it was still experiencing the feeling of carrying a mountain on its back.

Feeling angry for being bullied by two small rats, suddenly all the golden hairs on the Chimera's body stood up, blue lightning started shining in its eyes, and out of nowhere, a black cloud appeared in the close space of the dungeon, covering everyone's heads. Currently, his entire focus was on Pillow and her super hot body, like a pervert old uncle who saw a young girl on the road and couldn't hide his lust.

Thankfully, his wives stood behind; otherwise, he would have definitely earned a few slaps. But because of his hungry gaze, Pillow was continuously getting goosebumps, and she couldn't help but get closer to Xanadu, fearing that the next moment, Myne would rush to her and eat her alive.

This human is so disgusting. Why is he looking at me like I am some kind of food, and he can't wait to eat me, She thought while hugging herself. Years of staying with demons, she had long seen the super dark side of humans and knew what kind of creatures they are, but it was still hard for her to understand how there could be such a disgusting and perverted race out there.
"Cough, cough, this is hurt..."
"I told you to pay attention..."

Thankfully, maybe because of his weird situation, the weight on him lifted, and he could move freely. Only he didn't know where he was or what was going on.

First, Chimera used his skills, and after making sure everything was alright, he unfolded his giant wings and started flying. But everywhere he looked, there was just darkness and silence; nothing could be seen.
Only God knows how long he was flying, hungry and thirsty, tired as a dead dog. But finally, a ray of light shone in front of him.
The Chimera, just like a lost traveller in a desert seeing an oasis, desperately ran toward the light, and hope again ignited in his almost dead heart.

"Nice attack," was the only work the Chimera could mutter before its eyes rolled back and it lost its consciousness.
"Cool..."

"You damn bastard! Didn't you say you never practised secretly? Then where did this deadly attack come from? You just looked at him, and the other party was directly knocked out! What kind of cheating skill is this?" Waffle, as always, started complaining.

"This is not an ultimate attack, but my innate skill, 'Nether Eyes,' just like your 'Gravity Eyes.' You can control gravity, while I can seal someone's consciousness in a dark space and absorb all their mana until they lose all their consciousness," Ted explained while walking toward Myne and the other.

But what he didn't say was that he couldn't fully control this skill, which made it a double-edged sword, which is why he never used this before. Once someone's consciousness is sealed, he has no way to unseal it unless the other party automatically comes out. And there is also the risk of them permanently falling into a coma and losing their life.

"You... you... Just you two wait! I will show what I can do!" Waffle, who felt like he was being bullied, instantly exploded and decided that after this matter is over, he will rush to his mother and practice hard under her guidance and teach Ted and Myne a good lesson when he becomes powerful. No one can look down on a Divine Beast's child.

"We will see. Hopefully, you don't forget your words, and I don't find you lying on the couch when I wake up tomorrow," Myne didn't care about Waffle's outburst since it was nothing new, and he heard those words once every week. Instead, he looked at Xanadu, who was inspecting his "Pet" with an amazed look while rubbing his chin, seemingly in deep thought.

"I really underestimated those two little guys behind you. I never expected that they were someone with a rare bloodline, which I can't even detect. What a wonderful surprise. Now I am looking forward to winning this game and having some quality time with them," The more Xanadu looked at Waffle and Ted, who are still bickering in the background without paying his nonsense any attention, the more excited he became, just like a toddler who gets a new toy and couldn't wait to see what is inside it.

paragraphs: After the wonderful performance by Waffle and Ted, it was Aisha and Sylphy's turn to shine. Sadly, they were doomed to be in a difficult situation, as they were going to persuade Pillow the dark elf to switch to their side, and obviously, they couldn't simply beat their future ally to death.
[ Name: Paeallionara Aepallindril (Pillows)
Race: Elf ( Fallen into Darkness ) ( Dark Elf )
Gender: Female
Age: 583 y/o
Occupation: Slave ( Xanadu )
Divine Protection of The World Tree: Nature Blessings
Title: None
Status: Tired, Sad, Bored
[Skill]
Unique Magic: Wood
One-Handed Sword (Large)
Yggdrasil's Bind ]

"Are you girls absolutely sure you don't want me to cut off her skills? It could be very painful if she overpowers both of you and beats the hell out of you. Although she looks as young as you, don't be fooled. She's more than five hundred years old, and the experience gathered from all those years alone is enough to leave you two in despair," Myne asked worriedly.
However, his wives didn't take him seriously and casually waved their hands at him, telling him not to worry about them.
"Let's show him that we haven't just been lying around all this time and see how much we've improved," Aisha said calmly to Sylphy, who nodded and took out her long sword.

She and Aisha would practice in the backyard whenever they got a chance. Today, they finally had the opportunity to show Myne their power. How could they let him make their enemy lose all her skills? What was the difference between this and fighting an ordinary person without any skill? Wasn't it simply bullying the weak? Where was the dignity in that kind of thing?

"Although you knocked down Test Subject No. 1, which I think was a fluke, I don't feel as bad now, as Pillows here is one of the most powerful servants in terms of race. For that Hume woman, I don't think you'll stand a ghost of a chance," Xanadu said, showing a rare proud expression while patting on Pillow's back, encouraging her to beat the hell out of Aisha and Sylphy.

And Pillow, as a good servant, nodded seriously, walked forward, and without any useless nonsense, directly clapped her hands. With a whoosh, brown tree vines grew out from the ground and spread everywhere within a fifty-meter radius. They were followed by small white flower buds that appeared on the vines.
"This isn't looking good. Should we start pursuing her now or wait a bit?" Sylphy leaned against Aisha and whispered, having a bad feeling about those white flower buds.

"Let's show off our skills a bit before taking action; otherwise, that demon would have doubts. Now stop talking and use your fire magic to burn down those tree vines before they attack us," Aisha said.
Saying that, Aisha shot two arrows at Pillow, both aiming at her vital parts of the body. If she got hit, she would definitely lose her ability to fight or maybe even lose her life.

Sylphy also shot a dozen or so fireballs, about the size of an adult's fist, at the tree vines around them, and they burned. But to their surprise, although those vines were flammable, there was some kind of magic in them which quickly absorbed the flame, not letting it spread too far, and soon the burned vines recovered as new ones.

As for Pillow, seeing two arrows aiming at her heart and head rushing toward her, she didn't even blink. A wall made of tree vines grew in front of her, blocking both arrows before returning into the ground, clearing her view. Everything happened so neatly that people wondered if she did this kind of thing regularly.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
With a small banging sound, the flower buds on those tree vines opened one by one and released a pinkish gas from them, which soon covered the entire passage.

Unsurprisingly, the pink gas had no effect on Pillow and Xanadu, but it was a completely different matter for Myne's gang. They all felt an itching on their body. Myne, who had a Nightwalker's bloodline and was many times more powerful than most humans with extraordinary Endurance, also couldn't help but scratch. So you can imagine Aisha and Sylphy's condition: they are just normal humans, and right now, it's their strong willpower that keeps them on their feet. Otherwise, if it were someone else, he or she might have already been lying on the ground and scratching all over their body like a dog.
"We have to get rid of this gas quickly," Aisha said, gritting her teeth.

She quickly used her earth magic to create sharp spikes all around her, smashing a lot of flower buds, stopping them from releasing pink gas. Meanwhile, Sylphy madly shot fireballs around her without caring if those vines could regrow or not; she just wanted to get rid of this pink gas.

But while they were busy dealing with the pink gas, Pillow waved her hand, and an extremely gorgeous dark blade appeared in her slender hand, followed by a green glow. Tree vines grew around her and, like a snake, quickly covered her figure, and soon a beautiful full-body armour appeared, covering her and leaving nothing but her two beautiful dark eyes visible.

The armour, although looking fragile and easy to destroy, was not. It was very strong with a super-recovering ability and had dozens of small vines behind it that were like living tentacles, which could grow big as soon as Pillow thought and give the enemy a surprise attack. Those tentacle vines were very good at attack and support, making Pillow a close-combat genius.
This is odd. Something is wrong with these humans.
Speaking of the behaviour patterns of those who have seen our Demon races up until now, we have classified humans into roughly two types.
One type consists of barbarians who attack without reason, unable to gauge the difference in competence between them and us. The other would fear us and flee instantly upon seeing us.

However, the ones in front of me now are doing neither of those things. They show no fear at all, as if they didn't care about my existence, treating me as if I were just small fry they can kill at any time.
Even after knowing that I'm a Demon, they never lose their composure and are still treating me as a nobody.
It is an action that I would never have thought possible. I would assume the Hume race is arrogant, letting it get into their heads. There is something wrong with these people.
What on earth is going on? Do they simply not understand the meaning of facing a Demon? Or perhaps... are they absolutely confident in their ability to fight and kill me?
Either way, there is no doubt that this is completely different from most Humans I have seen.

What a sight. They have certainly faced a Disaster Grade monster, a Chimera. No matter if it's just two of them, how could such small creatures win against my creation? Hell Lord knows how much time I have spent modifying it. If it still loses to those two little ones, then I might as well hang myself.

The boy named Myne never doubted the victory of those two from the beginning. The look he gave me was the same as the Demon King, whom I had seen once; neither of them took everyone around them seriously and treated everyone as if they were watching ants. I hate that look.
Wait, a minute? A purple wolf? Now that I think about it, I believe I've heard of it somewhere, but I can't remember. It was a long time ago...
Hmm... No, it's useless. I can't recall. It seems I could remember if I pushed myself a little more. Well, there's no need to fret about it.

Well, Test Subject No. 1 is lost. Now I'm seriously doubting my life. How can those little guys have such a powerful body and recovery ability? Their injuries recover faster than an Ogre, and what is wrong with their skills? One can control gravity and the other consciousness! This doesn't make any sense. Just what the hell are their races? They are definitely not a wolf and a dog. This group of people are so weird.
Next is Pillows's turn. This woman was a good acquisition. Although she is extremely bad when it comes to sex despite being 500 years old, as a servant, she is good.

Her hatred of the Humans is real. If you possess this kind of hatred, you are usually supposed to be swallowed by it—you might end up losing yourself without any spiritual support and become a psychopath. But this has nothing to do with me... To me, she is just a tool, an extremely useful tool.
Although this woman has a deep hatred, she is a rare individual who can make situational judgments calmly.

High ability, good judgment, and what's more, a deep hatred... With these elements combined, there is no reason to lose to some Human women. Now, show your master what you're capable of! The depth of your anger! Your hatred!!!
But still believing a woman can finish your job perfectly is like smoking on a bomb site—not a wise decision. I'd better prepare Plan E. In any case, things don't seem to be going well recently...

However, the ones in front of me now are doing neither of those things.
They show no fear at all, as if they didn't care about my existence, treating me as if I were just small fry they can kill at any time.
Even after knowing that I'm a Demon, they never lose their composure and are still treating me as a nobody.
It is an action that I would never have thought possible.
I would assume the Hume race is arrogant, letting it get into their heads.
There is something wrong with these people.
What on earth is going on?
Do they simply not understand the meaning of facing a Demon?
Or perhaps... are they absolutely confident in their ability to fight and kill me?
Either way, there is no doubt that this is completely different from most Humans I have seen.
What a sight.
They have certainly faced a Disaster Grade monster, a Chimera.
No matter if it's just two of them, how could such small creatures win against my creation?
Hell Lord knows how much time I have spent modifying it.
If it still loses to those two little ones, then I might as well hang myself.
The boy named Myne never doubted the victory of those two from the beginning.
The look he gave me was the same as the Demon King, whom I had seen once; neither of them took everyone around them seriously and treated everyone as if they were watching ants.
I hate that look.
Wait, a minute?
A purple wolf?
Now that I think about it, I believe I've heard of it somewhere, but I can't remember.
It was a long time ago...
Hmm...
No, it's useless.
I can't recall.
It seems I could remember if I pushed myself a little more.
Well, there's no need to fret about it.
Well, Test Subject No.
1 is lost.
Now I'm seriously doubting my life.
How can those little guys have such a powerful body and recovery ability?
Their injuries recover faster than an Ogre, and what is wrong with their skills?
One can control gravity and the other consciousness!
This doesn't make any sense.
Just what the hell are their races?
They are definitely not a wolf and a dog.
This group of people are so weird.
Next is Pillows's turn.
This woman was a good acquisition.
Although she is extremely bad when it comes to sex despite being 500 years old, as a servant, she is good.
Her hatred of the Humans is real.
If you possess this kind of hatred, you are usually supposed to be swallowed by it—you might end up losing yourself without any spiritual support and become a psychopath.
But this has nothing to do with me...
To me, she is just a tool, an extremely useful tool.
Although this woman has a deep hatred, she is a rare individual who can make situational judgments calmly.
High ability, good judgment, and what's more, a deep hatred...
With these elements combined, there is no reason to lose to some Human women.
Now, show your master what you're capable of!
The depth of your anger!
Your hatred!!!
But still believing a woman can finish your job perfectly is like smoking on a bomb site—not a wise decision.
I'd better prepare Plan E.
In any case, things don't seem to be going well recently...

chapters.title: Chapter 762 - 762. One Side Beating
paragraphs: The fight between Pillow and Myne's two wives can only be described as one-sided bullying. After all, it's unrealistic to think that two 25-year-old girls could defeat an old antique with nearly 600 years of experience.

Unless someone provides Aisha and Sylphy with silent support and helps them win, even if Pillow spent her entire life eating, sleeping, and having fun, there is no way her control over her magic and skills could be something two little girls could compare to.

So, without even taking the fight too seriously, Pillow stood in the pink fog, fully clad in full-body armor made of magic vines, holding a magic sword. She watched Aisha and Sylphy scratching all over their bodies since the itching effect of the pink fog was too powerful. But thanks to their strong willpower and the effect of their ultra-regeneration skill, they were still able to hold on. Otherwise, anyone else in their place would have long ago been lying on the ground.

"Little brats of Hume, I do not have any grudge against either of you... It is just your bad luck that you were born as a Hume. So, let me kill you without having you suffer. It's the least I can do. If it's from my hands, you should be able to die safely, but if you fall into my master's hands, believe me, you will beg for death, but you will never receive that luxury," Pillow spoke coldly, with only her eyes visible through her helmet, as she slowly walked toward Sylphy, who was nearest to her.

It was supposed to be Sylphy and Pillow confronting each other in the center of the hall, two swordswomen playing with swords and sparks flying everywhere, but one party had already lost before the battle even began.

Sylphy felt like digging a hole and burying herself in it. She had never expected that Pillow, instead of fighting like a real swordsman, would use such a shameless method as using poison. She had no marital ethics at all.

"You shameless b*tch, you coward! If you have guts, then stop using those dirty tricks, and fight honestly!" Sylphy, whose face was already turning blue from anger, instantly exploded after hearing Pillow's words, and threw three football-sized fireballs at her.

"You are already getting bullied; I don't think provoking her further is a good idea, dear," Myne's hesitant voice sounded in Sylphy's mind, which she ignored with a cold snort. Obviously, she didn't take his advice, thinking that if it wasn't for the poisonous fog, she, along with Aisha, could easily teach the elf b*tch a good lesson.

However, Sylphy soon regretted her decision. Because her powerful fireballs, which could easily hollow out a thick tree, only created a loud bang and thick fog after colliding with Pillow's armor. But after the fog subsided, everyone's eyes widened, as there wasn't a single scratch on Pillow's armor. Obviously, this ordinary-looking vine armor was far from being ordinary.

While nodding with satisfaction upon seeing everyone's shocked expression, Pillow also moved toward Sylphy, ready to teach this ungrateful and insolent brat how to respect the elderly. Although, according to the elf lifespan standard, she was only about 40+ years old and couldn't be considered too old, a little girl who was no different than a toddler dared to speak disrespectfully to her and even curse her. How could she accept it? It was only natural for her to send her to her ancestors to vent the anger in her heart.
Bang!
Thud!
"In your next life, remember to be more respectful to someone who is older than you."

With a casual swing of her sword, she easily parried Sylphy's not-so-powerful sword attack, sending her sword flying away, and placed her own sword on Sylphy's neck. Staring at her coldly, Pillow wanted to see fear on her face, but to her surprise, Sylphy was still cursing her for being shameless under her breath, showing no sign of being desperate or fearful, which she should have, considering she was about to lose her life.

Just then, suddenly, two giant tornadoes appeared to the left and right of Sylphy and Pillow, absorbing all the pink fog before moving toward Xanadu. After reaching his side, they disappeared, letting all the pink fog cover his side.

Xanadu was a high-level demon, and the low-level poison had no effect on him at all. Since he wasn't a narrow-minded guy like most demons who easily lose their temper, he simply snorted coldly, thinking to write down this matter and punish them for it later.

In his mind, Myne and his gang had already become his experiment subjects. It was just a matter of time. If it wasn't for the fact that he was feeling too bored, having nothing interesting to do, he wouldn't have wasted his time on Myne and others at all; he would have simply captured them right after meeting them.
Pillow also looked behind Sylphy and saw Aisha putting down her arms, taking out her bow, and shooting an arrow at her. Obviously, she was the troublemaker who released those wind tornadoes.

In the end, I still have to help you two. Without me, what would you do? Sigh... Myne's voice, full of sarcasm, sounded in Aisha's head, making her want to beat him, but sadly, he was right. She had no way to refuse him. Without his help this time, she and Sylphy had no way to deal with Pillow's shameless magic attack.

Without the poisonous fog, Sylphy also recovered her fighting ability and quickly shot a dozen fireballs at Pillow while she was dealing with Aisha's arrows, distracting her. Sylphy quickly rushed toward her sword, picked it up, and charged at Pillow, ready to hack her to death.

"Did you say your name was Pillow? Why do you hate the Humes so much? Hypothetically speaking, if the Elves had a way to regain their livelihoods, what would you do?" Sylphy asked while slashing her sword at Pillow, who easily parried every attack. Obviously, she was a better swordsman than her.

"I never said my name, and why I hate Humes has nothing to do with you," While slashing horizontally and leaving a wound on Sylphy's arm, Pillow spoke coldly as she dodged five arrows Aisha shot at her, all of them aimed at her eyes.

She then made a fist with her left hand and slammed it hard on the ground. The next second, hundreds of vines shot out of the ground under Aisha's feet, who had been harassing her with arrows, forcing her to escape from those crazy vines that were chasing her like a tide.
"Now there are only two of us. Since you so desperately wanted to fight with a sword, let's see what you can do..."

"Myne, shouldn't you help them? It seems like they are getting bullied?" Waffle asked worriedly, watching Aisha desperately fighting with the crazy vines, but obviously, she was no match for those magic vines, and it was only a matter of time before she would get caught.

"But they refused to accept my help. Even though I still helped them deal with that poisonous fog, instead of being grateful, they didn't even say thanks to me. Why should I help these kinds of ungrateful people? Let them suffer. Anyway, they are not going to die. This is enough for me. Only when they get beaten will they learn their lesson and know my importance. They are taking me too lightly these days," Myne, while drinking a cold drink, spoke casually, enjoying watching Sylphy and Aisha getting beaten miserably.
To make things more enjoyable, he also had two magic eyes recording the whole process so he could make fun of them later. This kind of good material was too rare to let go.

"Aren't you worried they will vent their anger on you if they find out you're recording their shameful loss? They might not be able to beat this dark-skinned girl, but that doesn't mean they can't beat you. By the way, Aisha is looking at our side... I don't think she is in a good mood," Waffle, thinking about his dinner, continued taking Aisha and Sylphy's side, since if they got angry and refused to make dinner, where was he going to eat tonight?

"What? Did you say something? Sorry, it seems someone cast a skill on me. I can't see or hear anything... This is probably the demon cheating and attacking me. Damn this bastard!" Myne cursed loudly, but he showed no sign of moving and continued watching the show.

Just then, he saw a fountain of blood shooting into the air, and with a thud, Sylphy, with a long, deep sword wound from her right waist to her left shoulder, fell on her knees before dropping her sword with a disbelieving expression.

Pillow obviously didn't have the habit of leaving her enemies alive after beating them. After Sylphy fell to her knees, she raised her sword, ready to behead her beautiful head. But suddenly something happened that left her dumbfounded, and she couldn't help but look at Myne, who had been watching the fun since the start and had shown no intention of helping his teammates at all.

chapters.title: Chapter 763 - 763. Third Round
paragraphs: "Miss sexy, that's enough. Do you want to make me a widower at such a young age? She has already learned her lesson. Why don't you give me some face, let her go? Why don't you move to the other girl and beat her to half death as well? By doing this, you'll be giving me a big favour."

Myne's voice sounded in Pillow's mind, leaving her dumbfounded. At first, she didn't expect the girl who was talking nonsense all the time to be married. Even more bizarre was that her husband was actually using her to beat his wife and another teammate.
However, although Pillow was momentarily surprised by Myne's interruption, after coming back to her senses, she gave a disdainful snort before raising her sword, ready to end Sylphy's game.

"Now you're making things difficult for me. Don't think that just because that demon is backing you, you can do whatever you want. Try to hurt her a little bit and see if he can save your ass. Believe it or not, before that sword lands on my woman, your head won't be on your shoulders anymore." Myne's voice, filled with intense killing intent, again echoed in Pillow's mind, sending a chill down her spine.
Her battle instincts, honed through years of intense fighting, kicked in, warning her not to do anything funny, otherwise, she would definitely lose her life.

After hesitating for a moment, her deep desire to live finally won over her courage, and she lowered her sword under the confused gaze of Xanadu, who couldn't understand why his cold servant, who liked finishing all her opponents, let this human woman go. Pillow then headed toward Aisha, who was dodging her magic vines left and right, while continuing to communicate with Myne through telepathy.

"What the hell do you want from me? Since you're so powerful, why are you messing with a little character like me instead of fighting my master?" Pillow asked angrily. She hated this feeling of being toyed with by everyone and not having enough power to save herself.
"Because I want to save you. But before that, I want you to ask yourself why you're working with this demon and why you look so different from other elves."

This question had been bothering Myne from the beginning. It wasn't that he disliked it; he was just curious about the reason behind her transformation. As for her hatred toward humans, if someone destroyed his entire race for no reason, he would also hate them to death.

"To gain more power and protection from humans after my kingdom was destroyed, I had no other option except seeking help from those who hate humans. After all, the enemy of my enemy is my friend. I went to the demon kingdom and was accidentally captured by a powerful demon, who later sold me to a slave owner. I was then bought by my current master, who performed some experiments on me. Although this increased my power, it also gave me my current look, which I actually quite like," Pillow explained casually, not wanting to go too deep into the matter.

"I see. Then if, by chance, you lost your master and I provide you protection better than your current master, will you serve me as your new master?" Myne, who had long ago fixed his eyes on Pillow's breathtaking body, asked with a gentle smile.

"Acknowledging a human who destroyed my people and my family as my master and serving him? Not a chance. Even if you kill me, I will never bow before you, bastard," Pillow's high-pitched voice echoed in Myne's mind, leaving him dumbfounded. They had been chatting normally a moment ago, and the next moment the other party exploded. This was completely unexpected.
"Not even if I say I have a way to bring your race back to life?" Myne asked again with a smug tone, making Pillow's eyes widen.

"How can this be? This is impossible. You're talking nonsense. They all died long ago. They can't be revived," She spoke hurriedly, but seeing the smile on Myne's face from the corner of her eye so others wouldn't realise they were communicating, doubt began to form in her heart.
"By the way, do you know an elf named Amy?" Myne didn't reply directly and instead asked another question, creating even more confusion in Pillow's mind.
"How do you know Princess Amy?" She asked in shock, wondering if Myne was another elf disguised as a human.

"Amy is currently staying with me right now. Also, she's working hard to recover the life the elf race once had, which I mentioned earlier. We've already found a way to save your race. So now let me ask you again, do you still not want to acknowledge me as your new master?" Myne asked with a smile.

"...If what you said is true and you let me meet Princess Amy, then I am willing to become your slave, and do everything within my ability to serve you," Pillow said with determination while dodging arrows fired by Aisha. Because they didn't want to attract attention, Pillow continued pretending to fight Aisha with her magic.

"But as you can see, I might not be able to help you with anything right now. I'm just a slave and can't go against my master's orders. Even if you want me to cooperate, I don't think there's any room for discussion," She continued with a helpless sigh.

"It doesn't matter. Just defeat Aisha and finish this round. Leave the rest to me. Believe me, today you're going to change your master," Myne said confidently, if he can't even kill this low-level demon of his world, how can he make a foothold in other hellish gaming world?

Although Pillow still had some doubts, she did as asked. With a few casual waves of her arm, she summoned dozens more vines, overwhelming Aisha, an archer who wasn't good at close-range combat, and soon she was beaten unconscious.
But even to the very end, she didn't ask for Myne's help. It seemed Sylphy and Aisha truly wanted to become stronger instead of always relying on him.

"Well, well, well. Seems like this round is my win. Now we're at a draw," Xanadu said mockingly as Pillow returned to him. Although he was confused about why she didn't kill the two human women, considering his hatred for humans, he didn't think much of it, since they could be used as experimental subjects later.

"I think so too. But before we begin, considering your demon race's reputation, I want you to hand Pillow's slave contract over to me. What if you run away after losing? I've heard too many such stories," Myne said as he stood up from his chair and walked toward Xanadu.

"You have a point, but sorry, this won't work. What if I give you the contract and you run away? Don't forget, human reputation isn't much better than ours. Those arrogant elf bastards are the best example," Xanadu said while shaking his head.

"You've got a point. How about this? I give you fifty high-level monster cores, and you give me her contract. If I win, you return them to me. If you win, there's nothing to lose, you can simply take the contract from my body, right?" Myne said while taking out a bag full of monster cores from his inventory.

Nowadays, he never lacked money, and there was nothing worth spending it on anyway. The things he wanted were beyond the value of money in his world, so it was better to use it to fool this demon and get Pillow's slave contract. With that, she wouldn't be able to refuse any of his requests; slave contracts were no joke.
Xanadu fell into deep thought for a few seconds before nodding. With a wave of his hand, a golden parchment appeared, which he threw toward Myne. Myne did the same with the pouch of monster cores.
After examining the contract and confirming it was genuine, Myne put it away and looked at Xanadu, who seemed ready to make his move.
"Then..."
However, before Xanadu could start his nonsense, he was greeted by hundreds of fireballs raining down on him like meteors.
Continuous sounds of bombardment echoed throughout the dungeon and lasted for an entire minute before Myne stopped his fireball rain and waited for the dust cloud to settle.
"Cough, cough. Bastard, at least let me finish," Xanadu, completely unscratched by Myne's attack, waved his hand to clear the dust from his face and complained.

Suddenly, his entire body shone with dark red light. The next moment, he appeared in front of Myne. But his punch was faster than Myne could react. Myne was sent flying like a cannonball at extreme speed, smashing into the dungeon wall.
"Hmph. You humans really look down on us demons. Don't you know our magic resistance is no less powerful than those big lizards ( Dragon )...
BOOOM!

Xanadu didn't get the chance to finish his words again. Myne, moving three times faster than him, leaving a sonic boom behind, appeared in front of him and punched him in the face with an expressionless look.

Pillow, Waffle, and Ted, who were watching the fight, didn't even see how Myne appeared or how Xanadu disappeared. They only heard a loud bang from where Myne was supposed to be lying, followed by another loud bang where Xanadu had been standing.
Myne appeared out of thin air at his place, while Xanadu vanished, smashing into the wall behind him as if hit by a missile.

They had been chatting normally a moment ago, and the next moment the other party exploded.
This was completely unexpected.
"Not even if I say I have a way to bring your race back to life?" Myne asked again with a smug tone, making Pillow's eyes widen.
"How can this be?
This is impossible.
You're talking nonsense.
They all died long ago.
They can't be revived," She spoke hurriedly, but seeing the smile on Myne's face from the corner of her eye so others wouldn't realise they were communicating, doubt began to form in her heart.
"By the way, do you know an elf named Amy?" Myne didn't reply directly and instead asked another question, creating even more confusion in Pillow's mind.
"How do you know Princess Amy?" She asked in shock, wondering if Myne was another elf disguised as a human.
"Amy is currently staying with me right now.
Also, she's working hard to recover the life the elf race once had, which I mentioned earlier.
We've already found a way to save your race.
So now let me ask you again, do you still not want to acknowledge me as your new master?" Myne asked with a smile.

"...If what you said is true and you let me meet Princess Amy, then I am willing to become your slave, and do everything within my ability to serve you," Pillow said with determination while dodging arrows fired by Aisha.
Because they didn't want to attract attention, Pillow continued pretending to fight Aisha with her magic.
"But as you can see, I might not be able to help you with anything right now.
I'm just a slave and can't go against my master's orders.
Even if you want me to cooperate, I don't think there's any room for discussion," She continued with a helpless sigh.
"It doesn't matter.
Just defeat Aisha and finish this round.
Leave the rest to me.
Believe me, today you're going to change your master," Myne said confidently, if he can't even kill this low-level demon of his world, how can he make a foothold in other hellish gaming world?
Although Pillow still had some doubts, she did as asked.
With a few casual waves of her arm, she summoned dozens more vines, overwhelming Aisha, an archer who wasn't good at close-range combat, and soon she was beaten unconscious.
But even to the very end, she didn't ask for Myne's help.
It seemed Sylphy and Aisha truly wanted to become stronger instead of always relying on him.
"Well, well, well.
Seems like this round is my win.
Now we're at a draw," Xanadu said mockingly as Pillow returned to him.
Although he was confused about why she didn't kill the two human women, considering his hatred for humans, he didn't think much of it, since they could be used as experimental subjects later.
"I think so too.
But before we begin, considering your demon race's reputation, I want you to hand Pillow's slave contract over to me.
What if you run away after losing?
I've heard too many such stories," Myne said as he stood up from his chair and walked toward Xanadu.
"You have a point, but sorry, this won't work.
What if I give you the contract and you run away?
Don't forget, human reputation isn't much better than ours.
Those arrogant elf bastards are the best example," Xanadu said while shaking his head.
"You've got a point.
How about this?
I give you fifty high-level monster cores, and you give me her contract.
If I win, you return them to me.
If you win, there's nothing to lose, you can simply take the contract from my body, right?" Myne said while taking out a bag full of monster cores from his inventory.
Nowadays, he never lacked money, and there was nothing worth spending it on anyway.
The things he wanted were beyond the value of money in his world, so it was better to use it to fool this demon and get Pillow's slave contract.
With that, she wouldn't be able to refuse any of his requests; slave contracts were no joke.
Xanadu fell into deep thought for a few seconds before nodding.
With a wave of his hand, a golden parchment appeared, which he threw toward Myne.
Myne did the same with the pouch of monster cores.
After examining the contract and confirming it was genuine, Myne put it away and looked at Xanadu, who seemed ready to make his move.
"Then..."
However, before Xanadu could start his nonsense, he was greeted by hundreds of fireballs raining down on him like meteors.
Continuous sounds of bombardment echoed throughout the dungeon and lasted for an entire minute before Myne stopped his fireball rain and waited for the dust cloud to settle.
"Cough, cough.
Bastard, at least let me finish," Xanadu, completely unscratched by Myne's attack, waved his hand to clear the dust from his face and complained.
Suddenly, his entire body shone with dark red light.
The next moment, he appeared in front of Myne.
But his punch was faster than Myne could react.
Myne was sent flying like a cannonball at extreme speed, smashing into the dungeon wall.
"Hmph.
You humans really look down on us demons.
Don't you know our magic resistance is no less powerful than those big lizards ( Dragon )...
BOOOM!
Xanadu didn't get the chance to finish his words again.
Myne, moving three times faster than him, leaving a sonic boom behind, appeared in front of him and punched him in the face with an expressionless look.
Pillow, Waffle, and Ted, who were watching the fight, didn't even see how Myne appeared or how Xanadu disappeared.
They only heard a loud bang from where Myne was supposed to be lying, followed by another loud bang where Xanadu had been standing.
Myne appeared out of thin air at his place, while Xanadu vanished, smashing into the wall behind him as if hit by a missile.

chapters.title: Chapter 764 - 764. Unexpected Visitor
paragraphs: "How can he be so powerful?"

Pillow stared at Myne's figure with disbelief. She never expected that a human could be so powerful, that not only did he take a demon's full-power punch head-on and get up without a scratch, but his strength was far greater than a demon's, and that too without using any skill.

She couldn't even imagine what would happen if a strength-enhancement skill were cast on him and he went all out. She could swear, while patting her chest, that even by relying purely on his physique, he could go toe-to-toe with a dragon.
Myne unhurriedly walked toward Xanadu, who was struggling to get up. His face was dislocated by Myne's solid punch, and he was spitting blood continuously. Obviously, he was heavily injured.

"You talk too much. As a villain, this is not a good habit. Believe me, our villain profession has suffered a lot because of this bad habit," Myne said as he grabbed Xanadu's hair, lifted him up like doll, and punched him in the stomach so hard that he bent into a C-shape. He then threw him onto the ground. Because the other party spat saliva onto his arm, Myne kicked him hard, sending him flying away like a football.
"You demons always bully the weak. You've let your ego climb to your head. Do you really think there's no one who can beat your ass?"

"Hahaha! What about you? Don't you talk a lot as well?" Xanadu said as he struggled to get up, spitting another mouthful of blood. He took out a healing potion from his storage ring and drank it, then took another red potion and drank that as well.

"Didn't I tell you? This is like a curse. We villains, can't finish our enemies without talking nonsense," Myne said with a smile, then continued, "And I have confidence in my strength. I don't think that, as a fellow villain, you can suddenly gain mysterious power and turn the tables. That's a trait of a protagonist, and believe me, you're not one."

"I don't agree with that. I am the protagonist of my own story," As they spoke, the potion's effects began to show. Xanadu's body started heating up, steam rising from it. The next moment, before Myne realized what was happening, Xanadu appeared in front of him and punched hard at his face, ready to take revenge.

Pillow, who was watching the show, had a face full of excitement mixed with a hint of worry for Myne. He had given her hope that he could bring back all the dead elves, and even if he and Princess Amy were giving her false hope, she was more than willing to believe it rather than being toyed with by a demon without having any future of her own.

She didn't want to see Myne get killed. But when she saw Xanadu drinking a berserk potion, she couldn't help but widen her eyes. This was a modified potion that increased the drinker's physical strength three times for two minutes, with severe side effects, though not life-threatening.

If Xanadu, a demon with already amazing physical strength, took this potion, his strength could reach the point where he could single-handedly kill a dragon as if it were a random lizard. Against a human, it would be a one-hit kill.

She wanted to remind Myne to be careful, but before she could open her mouth, Xanadu had already made his move. He appeared before Myne as if he had teleported and punched him in the face, if that punch landed, Myne's head would explode like a watermelon.
But to her surprise, what happened next left her dumbfounded. Myne stood in place with a smug smile, while Xanadu was blasted away as if punched by an invisible hand and sent flying.

"No matter how many times I use it, this trick never fails to entertain me. It's really satisfying to let your enemy taste his own medicine, hehehe," Myne laughed while watching Xanadu get sent flying by his own punch.

When the other party was getting ready, Myne was already prepared to open a small portal in front of his face. As expected, Xanadu, like a wounded animal, rushed toward him to take revenge for punching his handsome face. His punch went straight into the portal he opened and came out beside his own face, blasting him away.
"That must've hurt a lot," Myne chuckled as he walked toward the other party, who had a dumbfounded expression, as if he couldn't accept his own defeat.

"Who the hell are you? How can you be so powerful? You can't be human! I've never seen such a powerful human in my entire life, and you weren't even using any skill. You shouldn't have this kind of body."

"This is beyond your racial limit, unless you modified your body or you're someone disguised as a human!" Xanadu said while staggering to his feet. His head was hurting like hell, and everything around him was spinning after taking his own enhanced punch at full power.
[ Special Attribute: Nightwalker Gene ]

"Well, I indeed can't be said to be fully human, Myne thought as he looked at his status. But there was no way he was going to explain this to anyone. He waved his hand, and the next moment, a hexagram array appeared above Xanadu.

The next moment, a pillar of lightning shot down from it and struck his head, completely devouring him. To end this one-sided battle, Myne used the full 100 points of mana, 80% of his total mana his body can store.

With such a crazy caliber of attack, anyone could guess Xanadu's end. No matter how high his magic resistance was, it had a limit. Once the attack crossed that limit, there was nothing more to say. The charcoal-like remains on the ground said everything.
"You look very miserable, Xanadu, being defeated and almost killed by a human. So pathetic. I wonder, if this information leaks, will you even be able to show your face in front of your king again?"

Just as Myne thought everything had settled and he could finally go back home, out of nowhere, from the shadow in the corner of the wall, a figure walked out and stood in front of Xanadu's injured, half-burned body.
Because of the potion he had drunk previously, his body was recovering very quickly. In just a few seconds, although he was far from being able to fight, he opened his eyes and struggled to stand up.
